igbo: Ọnwụ gbụ utu, gbụ eze; ihe agwụ, aka agwụsie.
english: Death kills the penis, kills the teeth; when a thing is exhausted, the hand is exhausted.
usage: When a man toils and saves, and grows old.
note: Restored 'Qiwu' as Ọnwụ and 'ife ageli ako agwusie' as ihe agwụ, aka agwụsie; Thomas's English is garbled.
igbo_raw: Qiwu gbug utu Bu çze; ife ageli ako agwusie (As.).
english_raw: Death kille penis, kils teeth ; a thing that can use property is When a man toils and saves, and grows old.

igbo: Asị ngwere, isi akịka eju gị; amaghị nke ga-acha.
english: They say the lizard's head is full of spots, but it does not know which will turn red-headed.
usage: A man has many children, no one knows who will get rich.
note: Restored 'ngwel' as ngwere, 'amwana' as amaghị, and 'gaca' as ga-acha.
igbo_raw: Asi ngwel' ísí akika eju gzi; amwana nke gaca
english_raw: akatankpo (I.A.). They say lizard has spots on head to fill a yard, but does not know who will türn red headed lizard. A man has many children, no one knows who will get rich.

igbo: A dighi ezute onye riri ụnya.
english: They never meet one who ate yesterday.
usage: To a thief who tries to rival a rich man by stealing.
note: OCR 'Adekwudo' read as A dighi ezute and 'niri nya' as riri ụnya; 'set out' in the English seems a misreading of 'ate'.
igbo_raw: Adekwudo onye niri nya (0.0.).
english_raw: They never meet one who set out yesterday. To thief who tries to rival rich man by stealing.

igbo: Ọ sị nwata, ị na-akwa akwa na nne gị jere ahịa madụ; ọ bụzi nke m ọ ga-esi mee?
english: He says to the child: 'You are crying that your mother went to the people's market; if she went to mine, how would it be?'
usage: Of a man who laments lack of money.
note: Moved the displaced 'nkemwo agesime?' into the proverb as nke m ọ ga-esi mee.
igbo_raw: Qsi nwata inakwakwa na nnei j'afia mwady, obuzia n'oje
english_raw: nkemwo agesime? (I.A.) He says to child you are crying that your mother went to man's market, if she went to mwg's, how would it be? Of a man who laments lack of money.

igbo: Ụwa adịghị mma madụ, ike eji nji.
english: If the world is hard for a man, his buttocks are black.
usage: A rich man does not talk of a poor man's troubles till the poor man talks of them.
note: Restored 'Enu adatylyka' as Ụwa adịghị mma and 'mwady' as madụ.
igbo_raw: Enu adatylyka mwady, íkè ejinye nji (I.A.).
english_raw: If the world is hard for a man, his buttocks are black. A rich man does not talk of a poor man's troubles till the poor man talks of them.

igbo: Ọ ka onye na-emeri onye iwe.
english: One who surpasses one, conquers him.
usage: A small man with money can purchase help.
note: 'onyêwe' is uncertain; it may be onye iwe or onye ya.
igbo_raw: Qka onye nem¢li onyêwe (Ala).
english_raw: One who surpasses one, conquers him. A small man with money can purchase help.

igbo: Ọnụ ite adịghị esi ite akpọ.
english: The neck of a pot does not break with the pot.
usage: A rich man leaves his property when he dies.
note: Restored 'ades'' as adịghị esi and 'akbp' as akpọ.
igbo_raw: Onu ite ades' ite akbp (Uk.).
english_raw: The neck of a pot does not break with the pot. A rich man leaves his property when he dies.

igbo: Ara dị okpọrọ n'obi adịghị ekwe ka nwoke wahapụ ya.
english: A woman's breast does not let men keep far from her.
usage: When a poor man depends on (sponges on) a rich man and won't be driven away.
note: The OCR 'enqëibe' is unclear; the restoration follows the English sense.
igbo_raw: Ala di okporho n'obi adekwe warhapu enqëibe (0.0.).
english_raw: A woman's breast does not let men keep far from her. When a poor man depends on (sponges on) rich man and won't be driven away.

igbo: Amadi adịghị ana ogbenye nwa.
english: A rich man does not take a poor man's child.
note: Read 'Amwadi' as Amadi and 'obwei' as ogbenye.
igbo_raw: Amwadi adana obwei nwa (0.0.).
english_raw: A rich man does not take a poor man's child

igbo: Ọ dị afị adịghị ana ogbenye nwa.
english: A rich man never takes away a poor man's child.
usage: A poor man can say this in misfortune.
note: 'Odafi' is uncertain; it may represent Ọ dị afị (one who has wealth).
igbo_raw: Odafi ádana obwei nwa (0.0.).
english_raw: A rich man never takes away a poor man's child. A poor man can say this in misfortune.

igbo: Ọnọdụ otu ebe na-ato ọla.
english: Sitting in one place makes one sleepy; riches make a man forget his fellows.
note: etiti may be 'ebe'; 'ọla' may be 'ụla' (sleep) with pun on 'ọla' (wealth).
igbo_raw: Qnodo ofu etiti nato ola (As.).
english_raw: Sitting in one place makes one sleepy. Riches make a man forget his fellows.

igbo: Anya adịghị onye ara ka ọ rie ngwere; ọ nweghị ụlọ ọ ga-eri ya.
english: A madman desires to eat a lizard; there is no house to eat it in.
usage: Not all can become rich.
note: Igbo reads 'anya adịghị onye ara...' (a madman has no eyes to eat a lizard), but Thomas's English 'desires' kept.
igbo_raw: Ainya adigo onye ala ka lie ngwele ; onebp ung oganozi lie (As.).
english_raw: A madman desires to eat a lizard; there is no house to eat it in. Not all can become rich

igbo: Eze kpere ikpe, ọ na-elo ọnụma; eze kwuputara ọnụma, ani agwụ n'aka ya.
english: The king complains, he stops vexation; if the king speaks out his wrath, the town finishes in his hand.
usage: When the rich oppresses the poor.
note: 'kbe ikße' read as 'kpere ikpe' (judges); Thomas's 'complains' kept.
igbo_raw: Eze kbe ikße, oiyalu gnuma, eze kwupute qnuma, ani agwua n' aka (Uk.).
english_raw: The king complains, he stops vexation; if the king speaks out his wrath, the town finishes in his hand. When rich oppresses poor.

igbo: Onye ji elu, ya kwaa ya rie; ya hapụ mma nwa ogbenye ji n'aka ya.
english: Whose yams are done, let him eat; let him leave the knife of the child of the poor man which he has in his hand to him.
usage: When the rich and the poor quarrel, the poor man says this.
note: 'ogali rwobwei' uncertain; reconstructed as 'mma nwa ogbenye'.
igbo_raw: Onye ji iyelu yakwalima, ya rhalu ogali rwobwei ji n'aka nye (Uk.).
english_raw: Whose yams are done, let him eat, let him leave knife of child of poor man which he has in his hand to him. When rich and poor quarrel, poor man says this. B 2

igbo: Nwa ọhụ amaghị onye kpụrụ isi ya.
english: A baby does not know who shaves its head; a rich man does not know the one who gave him a start.
note: Thomas's 'adamwa' read as standard 'amaghị'.
igbo_raw: Nwofo adamwa onye kwo isi (As.).
english_raw: A baby does not know who shaves its head. A rich man does not know the one who gave him a start.

igbo: Onye enweghị, mmadụ ibe enyeghị ya.
english: Who has none, others do not give to him.
usage: Said by a poor man with rich brothers.
note: 'Qiwe' read as 'enweghị'.
igbo_raw: Ónyé Qiwe, mw' Ibé éngê (Ala).
english_raw: Who has none, others do not give to him. By poor man with rich brothers.

igbo: Nke afụ onye adịghị afụ ibe.
english: What troubles one does not trouble another.
usage: A poor man has health, a rich man is sick.
igbo_raw: Nk'afy onye àdäfg ibe (Ala, Ubul.).
english_raw: What troubles one does not trouble another. A poor man has health, a rich man is sick.

igbo: Nke afụ onye adịghị afụ ibe.
english: What one suffers is not what his fellow suffers.
usage: A poor man cannot feed his children; a rich man has none to feed.
igbo_raw: Nke afy onye adafy ibe (Ubul.).
english_raw: What one suffers is not what his fellow suffers. A poor man can't feed his children, a rich man has none to feed.

igbo: Onye ọchụ gbuka mbada, mụ ụmụ anọ dị ibe.
english: The hunter kills many duiker but his four children are pawned.
usage: If a man complains that his share is small when he has not made a title.
note: 'Orhõe' read as 'Onye ọchụ'; 'umpa ang' as 'ụmụ anọ'; 'd'ibe' uncertain.
igbo_raw: Orhõe gbuka mbwada, mwa umpa ang d'ibe (Uk.).
english_raw: The hunter kills many duiker but his four children are pawned. If a man complains that his share is small when he has not made a title.

igbo: Isi anụ ka a na-afụ anya ya.
english: In the head of an animal they find its eyes.
usage: One in need goes to a rich man.
note: 'fasi afq' read as 'a na-afụ'.
igbo_raw: Isí anp ka fasi afq ainya (Uk.).
english_raw: In the head of an animal they find its eyes. One in need goes to a rich man.

igbo: Dị ka ogbenye, ọgụ ọjọọ ka ọ na-alụ.
english: So a poor man fights a bad fight, that is, with sticks, not money.
note: OCR and Thomas's transcription are badly damaged; Igbo restored from the English sense.
igbo_raw: Dig k' obwei afo njo pgo ano (Uk.).
english_raw: So a poor man fights bad fight, ie., with sticks, not money.

igbo: Ala adịghị ekpokọ egbu onye n'ihi ntụtụ isi ya dị elu.
english: The town does not gather to kill one because his hair is long.
usage: A rich man stays at home when he has palaver with another town; poor people go and die.
note: Restored 'egbu' and 'dị elu' from damaged OCR.
igbo_raw: Ani ádekoko elu onye na ntutße eluke (Uk.).
english_raw: The town does not gather to kill one because his hair is long. A rich man stays at home when he has palaver with other town; poor people go and die.

igbo: Ọhịa enyi na-abanye, mgbada na-abanyekwa n'ime.
english: The bush elephant walks in, the duiker also walks in.
usage: Rich and poor can both use the road.
note: Normalized the dialect verb and duiker name to standard forms.
igbo_raw: Ofia enyi akba, mbwada akbakwa n'ime (Uk.).
english_raw: The bush elephant walks in, the duiker also walks in. Rich and poor can both nse the road.

igbo: Nwoke adịghị oke na anụ kpuchie mbọ ya.
english: A man is not so stout that flesh covers his nails.
usage: No one is so rich that someone does not own him.
note: OCR badly damaged; Igbo restored from Thomas's English.
igbo_raw: Mwady adalwak' ofa K'obwakbo mbo dja n'aka (Uk.).
english_raw: A man is not so stout that flesh covers his nails. No one is so rich that someone does not own him.

igbo: Ọ bụ na ka ha gbusi nwa dibịa ka ha gbusi nwa ofeke?
english: They don't kill the child of a doctor and an ignoramus the same way.
usage: Rich and poor get different treatment.
note: Reconstructed as a rhetorical question; 'gesi' read as 'gbusi'.
igbo_raw: Qbuna ka wa gesi Bu rwa dibia ka wa gesi Bu iwa ofeke (Ubul.).
english_raw: They don't kill the child of a doctor and an ignoramus the same way. Rich and poor get different treatment.

igbo: Onye arịrịọ enweghị ihere.
english: A beggar has no shame.
igbo_raw: Onye aiyiyo eiu ifele (As.).
english_raw: A beggar has no shame.

igbo: Ụzọ ego adịghị mfe.
english: Getting money is not easy.
note: Thomas's 'efe' read as standard 'mfe'.
igbo_raw: Uzego adi efe (As.).
english_raw: Getting money is not easy.

igbo: Ogbenye na-ekwu okwu ka ọ dị ọrịa.
english: A poor man talks as if he were not well.
note: Read 'nçkwu' as 'na-ekwu' and supplied 'okwu' for sense.
igbo_raw: Obwenye nçkwu k'ary adjroa (As.).
english_raw: A poor man talks as if he were not well.

igbo: Onye eji dị n'olu amaghị na ọ na-eke ụcha.
english: He who has beads on his neck does not know that it shows its colour.
usage: If a rich man's son steals.
note: 'eji' taken as beads; 'uke' read as 'ụcha' (colour).
igbo_raw: Onye ejiji di onu amwarg n'oneke uke (Ubul.).
english_raw: Who has beads on his neck does not know that it shows its colour. If rich man's son steals.

igbo: Nwa mazi dị n'afọ bụ ọgbọ nwa ogbenye.
english: The son of a rich man in the womb is the same age as a poor man's son.
usage: A rich man's son is above a poor man who is older.
note: 'madi' read as 'mazi' (rich man); 'pbwg' as 'ọgbọ' (age mate).
igbo_raw: Nwa madi di n'afo bq rwambwei pbwg (Ala).
english_raw: The son of a rich man in the womb is the same age as a poor man's son. A rich man's son is above a poor man who is older.

igbo: Yamwa abụghị aha, nwa Ojei nwere iwe, wee gọọ aha.
english: Yamwa is not a name; the son of Ojei was angry and gave the name.
usage: When a man's sons all die, the father refuses to name another.
note: The final clause 'rha agoa' is uncertain; restored as 'wee gọọ aha'.
igbo_raw: Yamwa abun' afa, nwojei n'we, rha agoa (0.0.).
english_raw: Yamwa is not a name, son of Ojei was angry und gave name. When a man's sons all die, the father refuses to name another.

igbo: Anya na-aga n'ụzọ mmụọ na-eche onye nwe ya.
english: Eyes that go off wait for their owner on the spirit road.
usage: To a woman that loses her child.
note: Restored 'na-aga' and 'mmụọ' (spirit) from the OCR.
igbo_raw: Ainy' ainyuni non' uzg mwe e¢é onye rweni (0.0.).
english_raw: Eyes that go off wait for their owner on the spirit road. To a woman that loses her child.

igbo: Emume anaghị eji ịrụ ụkwụ apụ.
english: Trouble does not go away by shaking the leg.
usage: When a man worries his parents to buy things instead of working.
note: The verb for shaking the leg is uncertain; 'ịrụ ụkwụ' is the likely reading.
igbo_raw: Emuntuly adeji irurume ukwu ana (0.0.).
english_raw: Trouble does not go away by shaking leg. When a man worries parents to buy things, instead of working.

igbo: Eneke m ọbịa, sie nye ya nri.
english: To entertain a stranger, you cook and give him food.
usage: To a son-in-law who does not serve his father-in-law properly.
note: Restored 'ọbịa' and 'nri' from OCR 'obiai' and 'nni'.
igbo_raw: Enekem obiai sinyenni (0.0.).
english_raw: To entertain strangers you cook, give food. To son-in-law who does not serve father-in-law properly.

igbo: Ire mele, nwa atụrụ.
english: Tongue did it; Ilemele is a child of sheep.
usage: Ilemele was caught by ubido (tiger cat) because she would not keep silence at her mother's orders; used when a second in line, seeing a find on the road, makes it his own before the first can pick it up by saying 'abụ m.'
note: Restored 'ire' (tongue) and 'atụrụ' (sheep); 'abym' read as 'abụ m.'
igbo_raw: Ile mele nwa atulu (0.0.).
english_raw: Tongue did it (Ilemele) is child of sheep. (Ilemele was caught by ubido (tiger cat) because she would not keep silence at mother's orders.) When second in line seeing find on road makes it his own before first can pick it up by saying "abym."

igbo: A na-ato ilu, a naghị echefu ọnwụ.
english: They do not speak a proverb and forget death.
usage: A child does not forget his father's last words.
note: OCR 'az'' is probably 'ilu' (proverb), but the verb 'ato' may be 'ekwu'.
igbo_raw: Adamato az' qrwu (0.0.).
english_raw: They don't speak proverb and forget death. A child does not forget his father's last words.

igbo: Oyi na-atụ ihe, ọgọlọ nwanne ya na-atụ ihe.
english: A cold catches differently; harmattan, its brother, catches differently.
usage: A man's children are not all the same.
note: Restored 'oyi' (cold) and 'ọgọlọ' (harmattan) from the OCR.
igbo_raw: Vyi atu iõe, ogolo rwanne atu iëe (0.0.).
english_raw: A cold catches differently, harmatan, his brother, catches differently. A man's children are not all the same.

igbo: Nwata nọ n'ụzọ na-akọcha onye na-aga ije; na-atụkwasị obi na nna ya nọ nso.
english: A child stands by the way and abuses passers-by; he trusts that his father is near.
note: Restored 'na-akọcha' (abuses) and 'na-atụkwasị obi' (trusts).
igbo_raw: Nwata no n'ezi yzQ, nakbg onye kani iku ; degkunie nna naiva noiva nso (Ala).
english_raw: Child stands by the way and abuses passers by; he trusts that his father is near.

igbo: Otu nwa amaka n'ụbọchị egwu; ọ bụrụ na nsogbu bịara, ọ na-akwa.
english: One child is good on the day of a dance; when trouble comes he cries.
usage: A man wants all good things for his child; in the day of trouble he can bear it alone.
note: The second clause is reconstructed from the English; OCR 'obgsi yagami pkwa' is uncertain.
igbo_raw: Ofu rwa amaka ybosi egu; obgsi yagami pkwa (0.0.).
english_raw: One child is good on the day of a dance; when trouble comes he cries. A man wants all good things for his child; in the day of trouble he can bear it alone.

igbo: Ihe a naghị ahụ n'ọrị nne ewu, a naghị ahụ n'ọrị nwa.
english: Things not seen in the vulva of the goat, they will not see in that of the child.
usage: The son will not accept treatment his father would not allow.
note: Restored 'ọrị nne ewu' (vulva of the mother goat) and 'ọrị nwa' (that of the child).
igbo_raw: Ife anafurg n'ory nnewhu wamafoa na nke nwa (0.0.).
english_raw: Things not seen in vulva of the goat they will not see in The son will not accept treatment his father would not allow.

igbo: Ọ bụghị na ara wakpọrọ, ka ọ na-ada.
english: It is not the day breasts develop that they fall.
usage: When children advise parents.
note: The OCR forms obgsi and Ila are uncertain; the proverb is read from the English and likely Asaba/Ika shape.
igbo_raw: Qbuna obgsi wakbom' Ila, k' oda (I.A.).
english_raw: It is not the day breasts develop, that they fall. When children advise parents.

igbo: Ibudu adịghị ada nọ n'elu.
english: A trap on the ground cannot fall on an animal if it is in a tree; a boy cannot know more than his father.
note: adadebu is resolved as adịghị ada, and gno as nọ.
igbo_raw: Ibudu adadebu gno n' enu (As.).
english_raw: A trap on the ground cannot fall (on an animal) if it is in a tree. A boy cannot know more than his father.

igbo: Ha adịghị agụ akwa ọkụkọ amụ ọkpa.
english: They never consider an egg to know the cock; a child does not know more than his father.
note: ádang is read as adịghị agụ, and gkba as ọkpa.
igbo_raw: Wa ádang akwa okoko amwa gkba (Uk.).
english_raw: They never consider an egg to know the cock. A child does not know more than his father.

igbo: Mmiri adịghị aka onye nwe ụlọ amụ ihe.
english: Rain does not know better than the householder; a child is not wiser than its father.
note: The cross-reference to item 667 is omitted from the meaning.
igbo_raw: Mili adaka onye nwe uno amwa ife (I.A.).
english_raw: Rain does not know better than householder. See 667. A child is not wiser than its father.

igbo: Ege dị okpo adịghị mma ibu aja; ọ bụ isi ga-ebu ya.
english: The flower of okpo is not good for carrying sacrifice; it is the head that will carry it.
usage: When a son asks his father to buy a wife, when he has no money.
note: adigummwa is read as adịghị mma, and the English 'is good' is taken as damage for 'is not good'.
igbo_raw: Ege d' okpo adigummwa ibu aja gneby k' isi gesilu ebu
english_raw: (I.A.). Flower of okpo is good for bearing sacrifice, it is the head will carry it. When a son asks his father to buy a wife, when he has no money.

igbo: Ọdịda adịghị ewepụ ihe dị n'afọ; onye dara ebulu nke ya bili ọtọ.
english: Falling does not throw away things in the stomach; who falls takes up his and stands up.
usage: (a) If a child speaks without being asked. (b) Strangers don't understand each other as friends do.
note: Reconstructed from badly damaged OCR; the opening bracket and nisi oto remain uncertain.
igbo_raw: (Ada) Adada ewu(si)fu ife diafo; onye dada obulu nke
english_raw: nisi oto (I.A.). Falling does not throw away things in stomach; who falls takes up his and stands up. (a) If child speaks without being asked. (b) Strangers don't understand each other as friends do.

igbo: Aka nri ka eji eti nwa; aka ekpe ka eji adụ n'anya.
english: The right hand they take to beat a child; the left they take to caress.
usage: An enemy may say "flog," but he does not replace a dead child.
note: akanni is restored as aka nri and akgkbe as aka ekpe.
igbo_raw: Akanni ka waji eti rwa; akgkbe ka waji ad'ainya n° ary (Ala).
english_raw: The right hand they take to beat child; the left they take to caress. An enemy may say "flog," but he does not replace a dead child.

igbo: Mgbe nna m dị ndụ, anyị adaghị ahụ nsogbu; nna bụ chi onye.
english: When my father was alive, we did not see trouble; a father is a man's chi.
usage: The son suffers when his father dies.
note: ci is read as chi, and ainyi adafiyà as anyị adaghị ahụ.
igbo_raw: Aina ba dindo ainyi adafiyà nna buèi onye (Ala).
english_raw: When my father was alive, we did not see trouble, his father is a man's ci. The son suffers when his father dies.

igbo: Onye nwere nwa jọrọ njọ agaghị ewe okpokoro gbuo ya.
english: He who has a bad child cannot take wood to kill him.
usage: When people complain to a father of his child.
note: Nwa onye jo anjo is read as Onye nwere nwa jọrọ njọ, and ti Buye as gbuo ya.
igbo_raw: Nwa onye jo anjo gmawe okbokBo ti Buye (0.0.).
english_raw: Who has a bad child can't take wood to kill him. When people complain to a father of his child.

igbo: Ha adịghị eji isi awọ amụ ihe.
english: They do not take grey hair to know something.
usage: (a) If a child learns much from father and grows wise in youth. (b) Elders must consult younger men also. Cf. 520.
note: Fadeji is expanded as Ha adịghị eji.
igbo_raw: Fadeji isi awo amwa ife (0.0.).
english_raw: They do not take grey hair to know something. (a) If child learns much from father and grows wise in youth. (b) Elders must consult younger men also. Сf. 520.

igbo: Ọsa hụrụ aha, agụọ aha nwa.
english: If the squirrel sees a name, it names a child.
usage: When a man admires a rich man's house (and has no money to build in the same way).
note: OCR 'Qsa fu afa agona iwa' restored; final 'iwa' taken as nwa.
igbo_raw: Qsa fu afa agona iwa (0.0.).
english_raw: If squirrel sees a name, he names a child. When a man admires rich man's house (has no money to build in same way).

igbo: Ọ nọ ala, akpata igwe aka.
english: He sits down and touches the sky.
usage: A rich man sends and his work is done.
note: OCR 'Qnp ani' read as Ọ nọ ala.
igbo_raw: Qnp ani akpat' igwe aka (0.0.).
english_raw: He sits down and touches the sky. A rich man sends and his work is done.

igbo: Ụwa agwụghị.
english: The world does not finish; your children may suffer for you.
usage: If a rich man harasses a poor man for nothing.
note: OCR 'Ow(a) ägwunà' normalized to Ụwa agwụghị; parenthetical placed in the English meaning.
igbo_raw: Ow(a) ägwunà (0.0.).
english_raw: The world does not finish. (Your children may suffer for you.) If a rich man harasses a poor man for nothing.

igbo: Iyi atara, obodi egbu azụ n'elu ugwu.
english: The stream dries up, a fool kills fish on the hill.
usage: Good things always go to the rich.
note: OCR 'ebu azp n'enugu' read as egbu azụ n'elu ugwu.
igbo_raw: Iyi àtá, obodi ebu azp n'enugu (0.0.).
english_raw: The stream dries up, a fool kills fish on the hill. Good things always go to the rich.

igbo: Ogbenye nwere enyi, ọdara anara ya.
english: The poor man gets a friend; the rich man takes him away.
note: OCR 'odafi analaiya' read as ọdara anara ya.
igbo_raw: Óbwei nwura oii; odafi analaiya (0.0.).
english_raw: The poor man gets a friend ; the rich man takes him away.

igbo: Ntakịrị adịghị agwụ n'gbọọlọ onye na-ata ọchị.
english: A little palm wine stops in the calabash of the palm wine maker.
usage: A rich man is never reduced to poverty.
note: OCR 'Cakadaka ädäkg n' gbwqlg di oci' restored; 'oci' taken as ọchị.
igbo_raw: Cakadaka ädäkg n' gbwqlg di oci (As.).
english_raw: A little palm wine stops in the calabash of the palm wine maker. A rich man is never reduced to poverty.

igbo: Ewu adịghị ata igu, ata ekwele.
english: A goat does not bite palm leaves and bite ekwele (tie-tie) at once.
usage: A poor man's child cannot leave its father and go to a rich man.
note: Restored adịghị; 'igu' is Thomas's palm-leaf word, 'ekwele' is tie-tie.
igbo_raw: Ewu adata igu, at' ekwele (As.).
english_raw: A goat does not bite palm leaves, and bite ekwele (tie-tie) (at once). A poor man's child cannot leave its father and go to a rich man

igbo: Ụwa dị iche iche.
english: The world is varied.
usage: A woman may be rich and good-looking but have no children.
note: OCR 'Owa' and 'ice ice' restored to Ụwa dị iche iche.
igbo_raw: Owa di ice ice (0.0.).
english_raw: The world is varied. A woman may be rich and good-looking but have no children.

igbo: Ọ dịghị onye na-atụgharị ihu karịa onye anwụrụ ọkụ na-egbu.
english: No one turns his face more than the one that smoke hurts.
usage: One who has means of livelihood is better off than one who has none.
note: OCR 'WadeBiru akali ony'arwolo emg' is badly corrupted; restored from English and known proverb.
igbo_raw: WadeBiru akali ony'arwolo emg (0.0.).
english_raw: No one turns his face more than the one that smoke hurts. One who has means of livelihood is better off than one who has none.

igbo: Onye mgba adịghị agba na onye nwe ụlọ.
english: A wrestler does not wrestle with the owner (father) of the house.
usage: A man must not quarrel with his master.
note: OCR and Ala-dialect spelling badly damaged; the second Ala variant in the entry is omitted.
igbo_raw: Ybwambwa adabwa' gdafe eba (Ala).
english_raw: A wrestler does not wrestle with the owner (father) of the house. Okambwa bw' gdaf' eba; mbia obul' omy (Ala). If a wrestler strives with the owner of the house; he starves. A man must not quarrel with his master.

igbo: Ụwa bụ otu a.
english: The world is this (such is life).
usage: When a man finds servants neglecting their work.
note: OCR 'Enu bu qrwy' restored as Ụwa bụ otu a; 'Enu' is uncertain.
igbo_raw: Enu bu qrwy (0.0.).
english_raw: The world is this. (Such is life.) When a man finds servants neglecting their work.

igbo: Ọzọ bụ aba; dibịa na-asa ya.
english: A blacksmith makes a staple; the doctor washes it.
usage: Of a man who boasts of knowing more than his master.
note: Restored 'dibịa na-asa ya' from Thomas's 'dibia déa'; 'ọzọ' is blacksmith.
igbo_raw: Ozo bu aba ; dibia déa (0.0.).
english_raw: A blacksmith makes a staple; the doctor washes it. Of a man who boasts of knowing more than his master.

igbo: Odibo abụ eze bụ eze ọfụma; odibo bụa eze n'abụọ, ọ lịe.
english: A servant serves a king, he serves the king well; a servant serves two kings, he is true to one.
note: Restored 'çz' and 'ofuma' to eze and ọfụma; 'olie' read as ọ lịe, and the stray 'ivi ofu' treated as OCR noise.
igbo_raw: Odibo abw' eze bw'çz ofuma; odibo bwa eze nabo, olie
english_raw: ivi ofu (0.0.). A servant serves a king, he serves the king well; a servant serves two kings, he is true to one.

igbo: Agene adaghị n'elu akpọ Lokọja.
english: A native mat never lies on a Lokoja mat; a man is less than his master.
note: Restored 'abwakpo ole' to n'elu akpọ Lokọja from the English 'Lokoja mat'.
igbo_raw: Agene adà abwakpo ole (0.0.).
english_raw: Native mat never lay on LokoЇa mat. A man is less than his master.

igbo: Onye nwe egede kpọpụọ ya, ọ dịghị ajọ njọ.
english: Who has a drum and bursts it, it is not bad; an owner is not blamed.
note: Restored 'nve' to nwe, 'pda' to ọ dịghị, 'ajgnje' to ajọ njọ; 'kBopue' read as kpọpụọ.
igbo_raw: Onye nve egede kBopue pda ajgnje (Ubul.).
english_raw: Who has a drum and bursts it, it is not bad. An owner is not blamed.

igbo: Ụbọchị onye nwe ụlọ tiwara ụkọ, ka oge eruzu; nwata tiwara ya, a kụọ ya ihe.
english: The day the owner of a house breaks a calabash, its time has come; a child breaks it, they flog him; an owner is not blamed.
note: Restored 'etiwe' to tiwara, 'çzu' to eruzu, 'qbue imi' to kụọ ya ihe; 'gdafi' read as onye from context.
igbo_raw: Obosi gdafi nwe ung etiwe uko k' oge çzu; nwata tiwe qbue imi (Ubul.).
english_raw: The day the owner of a house breaks a calabash, its time is come; a child breaks it, they flog him. An owner is not blamed.

igbo: Onye nwe ike ịti aka.
english: Who has buttocks can slap them; an owner is not blamed.
note: Restored 'Onwe' to Onye, 'fke' to ike, 'gti' to ịti.
igbo_raw: Onwe fke gti aka (Ubul.).
english_raw: Who has buttocks can slap them. An owner is not blamed.

igbo: Nkịta adịghị abọ n'ebe onye nwe ya.
english: A dog does not bark at his master.
note: Restored 'adabo' to adịghị abọ and 'dinwenia' to n'ebe onye nwe ya.
igbo_raw: Nkita adabo dinwenia (As.).
english_raw: A dog does not bark at his master.

igbo: Mmadụ ma nwe ndụ, mmiri ọnụ anaghị eti ya n'ihu eze.
english: If a man has life, the rain (? saliva) will not beat the front of his teeth.
usage: A child of a rich man will not go under in a palaver.
note: Thomas's 'ebwebwe' and 'anamwa' are uncertain; the reconstruction follows his English and the known proverb shape.
igbo_raw: Mwady ama nweke ebwebwe n' gnu mili anamwa n'iru eze (Ubul.).
english_raw: If a man has life, the rain (? saliva) will not beat the front of his teeth. Child of rich man will not go under in palaver.

igbo: Ngwụrọ abụọ na-eje n'ụzọ ije, gburu nnụ anọ ijiji.
english: Two lame men walking in the road killed four hundred flies.
usage: If two rich men travel, each makes his own arrangements.
note: 'nnụ ijiji' is literally hundred flies; Thomas's 'four hundred' may reflect a larger numeral not fully legible.
igbo_raw: Qkûmn nabp iyili n'ozg ie, webde nno ijiji (As.).
english_raw: Two lame men walking in the road, killed four hundred flies. If two rich men travel, each makes his own arrangements.

igbo: Anyị je n'ebe ọgaranya, ka anyị bụrụ; onye je n'ebe ogbenye akalị mma.
english: We go to the house of a rich man that we may become so; he who goes to a poor man is better off.
usage: The poor are more generous than the rich.
note: 'odafe' is read as ọgaranya and 'obwei' as ogbenye; 'akalimwa' is normalized to akalị mma.
igbo_raw: Ainyi je b' odafe, k'ainyi by; onye je b'obwei akalimwa (Ala).
english_raw: We go to the house of a rich man, that we may become so; who goes to poor man is better off. The poor are more generous than the rich.

igbo: Ọjịrị anaghị atụfu ego, ọ na-ada ogbenye mgbe ọ nwụrụ.
english: A rich man does not throw away money; he is poor when he dies.
note: Thomas's transcription is too damaged to recover verbatim; the Igbo is reconstructed from the English and from 'ọjịrị'.
igbo_raw: Iyi okbak' ute, mwa ójirg agene lu mwe (As.).
english_raw: A rich man (a) does not throw away money, (b) is poor when he dien.

igbo: Nwa nze dị afọ bụ nwanne ogbenye gbụọ.
english: The son of a rich man in the womb is the companion of a poor man.
usage: A rich man's son has advantages.
note: The final 'gbụọ' is uncertain, and 'Uf. 421' appears to be a cross-reference.
igbo_raw: Nwanze di afg bu rwambwei gbwg (0.0.).
english_raw: The son of a rich man in the womb is the companion of a poor man. A rich man's son has advantagen. Uf. 421.

igbo: Ọ na-atụkọ tụkọ, adịghị atụ nke nne n'ahịa.
english: He can distinguish footsteps well, he cannot distinguish his mother's in the market.
usage: The son of a rich man does not know how his father became rich.
note: 'tụkọ tụkọ' and 'n'obwe' (market) are restored with some doubt.
igbo_raw: Oka túke tüke, adetu te okunne n'obwe (As.).
english_raw: He can distinguish footsteps well, he cannot distinguish his mother's in the market. The son of a rich man does not know how his father became rich.

igbo: Onye mụtara adịghị aka onye nkuzi.
english: A learner is not greater than his teacher.
note: Normalized Thomas's 'muta' and 'adiaka' to mụtara and adịghị aka.
igbo_raw: Onye muta adiaka onye nkuzia (As.).
english_raw: A learner is not greater than his teacher.

igbo: A dịghị ama ihe ha na-asị ọgọ.
english: They don't know what they say to a relative-in-law.
usage: Go slow with your superior.
note: Thomas's 'Adewa mwaly' is badly damaged; read provisionally as A dịghị ama.
igbo_raw: Adewa mwaly ife wa asja 089 (Uk.).
english_raw: They don't know what they say to relative-in-law. "Go slow with your superior."

igbo: Ọ bụghị na osisi nwere ọtụtụ akọtụ ka ọ na-amị ihe a na-eri.
english: It is not because a tree has many roots that it bears a thing they eat.
usage: Inferiors stand when a superior comes, even if he is a small man.
note: Restored 'abwakotu' as nwere ọtụtụ akọtụ per the English.
igbo_raw: Qbuna n'osisi abwakotu k' Oji am(1) if oweli (0.0.).
english_raw: It is not because a tree has many roots that it bears a thing they eat. Inferiors stand when a superior comes, even if he is a small man.

igbo: Ọ ka onye, a na-enye ya ola.
english: He surpasses one and forces old food (yesterday's) on him.
note: Thomas's 'abwainye' is uncertain; read provisionally as a na-enye ya.
igbo_raw: Qk' onye abwainye ola (0.0.).
english_raw: He surpasses one and forces old food (yesterday's) on him.

igbo: Ọgọ adịghị egbu ọgọ, anyị amaghị onye ha gbanyere ya.
english: A father-in-law does not kill his son-in-law; we don't know for whom they forbid it.
usage: Son-in-law does not inform against father-in-law.
note: Read 'wasginyaiya' as ha gbanyere ya, with some uncertainty.
igbo_raw: Qgò adeBu ggoa ainyi amwarg onye wasginyaiya (Ubul.).
english_raw: A father-in-law does not kill his son-in-law, we don't know for whom they forbid it. Son-in-law does not inform against father-in-law.

igbo: Osisi na-asị ala na ọ dị ochie, anyị amaghị ebe ọ si pụta.
english: A tree that says to the ground he is older, we don't know where it grows from.
usage: When a child rebukes his father.
note: Normalized 'ani' to ala and 'oi' to ochie.
igbo_raw: Osisi nasi' ani naiya dj oi, na ainyi amwazi ebe osipu (Uk.).
english_raw: A tree that says to the ground he is older, we don't know where it grows from. When a child rebukes his father.

igbo: Oke adịghị eji ọdụ etiwa ite
english: A rat does not take its tail to break a pot.
usage: A child cannot cohabit with its mother.
note: Restored adịghị eji ọdụ etiwa; 'cohabit' is retained as Thomas wrote it, though the usage note is odd.
igbo_raw: Oke àde w' odo etiwe ite (Uk.).
english_raw: A rat does not take its tail to break a pot. Child cannot cohabit with mother.

igbo: Nwata amaghị ụbọchị a mụrụ nne ya
english: A child does not know the day his mother was born.
usage: A child cannot act ill to his mother's people, because he may have to run to them.
note: Thomas's 'mwáli mwali mwali' is badly damaged; restored to the known proverb.
igbo_raw: Nwata mwáli mwali mwali (Uk.).
english_raw: A child does not know the day his mother was born. A child cannot act ill to his mother's people (because he may have to run to them).

igbo: Agwọ pịa nwa ya, sị ha, weta nwa agwọ ahịhịa ka ha gbue
english: The snake bites its child, says to them: bring the child of a grass snake to kill.
usage: When A hides the misdeeds of his own child and exposes those of B's.
note: Read 'psifa' as sị ha and 'olila' as ahịhịa; 'keeps' corrected to 'bites' from pịa.
igbo_raw: Agwo pia rwa psifa wete nkq olila kafaBulie (Ubul.).
english_raw: The snake keeps a child, says to them: bring the child of a grass snake to kill. When A hides misdeeds of his own child and exposes those of B's.

igbo: Ife ha ji agọ nwa ka ha ji agọ nwa, ha adịghị eji ọtọ agọ nwa
english: What they take to coax a child, they take; they never take a woman's genitals to coax a child.
usage: Husband to wife: don't praise a bad son.
note: Restored ha ji agọ and adịghị eji; 'ọtọ' is retained as Thomas's 'woman's genitals'.
igbo_raw: Ife faji agogo rwa ka waji agogo nwa, fa deji oto agogonwa (Ubul.).
english_raw: What they take to coax child, they take; they never take woman's genitals to coax child. Husband to wife: don't praise bad son.

igbo: Nne mbe na-ebu okpokoro, nwa ebulu na-ebu ajị
english: The mother of the tortoise wears a shell and her child wears hair.
usage: A child cannot say to his father that he copulates with more women than his father, including his mother.
note: Thomas's 'amabu' and 'agele' are uncertain; I read them as na-ebu and ajị, but the English 'does not wear' may preserve a negative form.
igbo_raw: Nne mbeku amabu okbulukbu nwa ebulu agele (Ubul.).
english_raw: The mother of the tortoise does not wear a shell and her child wear hair. Child cannot say to father he copulates more women than his father, including his mother.

igbo: Nkpo dị n'ife, ma ọ dịghị n'ife; ọ na-akọ n'anya ọkụ
english: A round basket is useful or useless; it hangs over the fire.
usage: A man must not drive his family out.
note: Restored nkpo and ma; 'okolo' read as ọ na-akọ.
igbo_raw: Nkpodo di n'ife mwa odiro n'ife; okolo n'ainya oky (Ubul.).
english_raw: A round basket is useful or useless; it hangs over the fire. A man must not drive his family out.

igbo: Ozi onye na-abụ, ka e ji agụ eyi.
english: Who teaches singing is imitated; a family imitates its head.
note: Restored from a damaged transcription; 'agụ eyi' may be a dialect form for imitation, and the exact proverb remains uncertain.
igbo_raw: Ozi onye aby, k' oji gny eyi (Ubul.).
english_raw: Who teaches singing, is imitated. A family imitates its head.

igbo: Abụlụ aka ọdọ, abụlụ nne.
english: If you take the mortar, take the pestle; if a wife is taken by force, take the child too.
note: Thomas's 'nne' may stand for 'nwa' or the second pair is compressed; 'aka ọdọ' is the pestle.
igbo_raw: Abul' ak' odò abulu nne (As.).
english_raw: If you take the mortar, take the pestle. If a wife is taken by force, take the child too.

igbo: Etete n'aka bụ ụwa.
english: Softly and careful is the world.
usage: To rebuke wild children.
note: OCR 'by enu' read as 'bụ ụwa' and 'akg' as 'aka'.
igbo_raw: Etete n' akg by enu (0.0.).
english_raw: Softly and careful is the world. To rebuke wild children.

igbo: Chibụọzọ sị ewụ mmadụ na-akwa m, ma nke ya sị nyem akpụji.
english: Chibụọzọ says other people's goat cries at me, but his own says give me seed yam.
usage: When a man's own family are backward and unorderly.
note: Name and dialect words restored; 'mwad'' read as 'mmadụ' and 'akbuji' as 'akpụji'.
igbo_raw: CiB pzg si çwu mwad' nea alia me me nke n'alia so n'aka myem akbuji (Ubul.).
english_raw: Cib' ozo says other people's goat cry me, but his say give me seed yam. When a man's own family are backward and unorderly.

igbo: Amụtara m ihe adịghị ekwe, ọgụlụgụ adị m.
usage: To one who refuses parents' advice. See 728.
note: Only the usage note survives clearly; the proverb's second half is unrecoverable from OCR.
igbo_raw: Amwakam ife adekwe ogulugu ädd (0.0.).
english_raw: To one who refuses parents' advice. See 728.

igbo: Nwayọ bụ ije.
english: Slow and sure.
usage: To a child that is in a hurry or violent.
igbo_raw: Nwaiyo bu ije (0.0.).
english_raw: Slow and sure. To a child that is in a hurry or violent.

igbo: Ọlọlọbwọ sị nwata ya, Egbukwena ya, n'afọ atọ ka i jaa.
english: Ọlọlọbwọ says to his child, do not kill me, for three years you take to cut him up.
usage: Warning to a child not to violate customs.
note: The OCR is severely corrupt; the Igbo is a tentative restoration from Thomas's phonetic spelling and English sense.
igbo_raw: Qlolobwo si rwata ya ¿Bukweneya n' arh'ato k' ija
english_raw: buya (O.0.). Olgigbwo says to child don't kill me, for three years you take to cut him up. Warning to child not to violate customs.

igbo: Ịbụ ibu ka mmadụ agwa nwa ya na-aga gafee obodo.
english: If you get trouble you carry it, as a man said to his son who was going out in the town.
usage: Warning to child.
note: Thomas's 'ibure ibulu' and 'nojekg' are read as ịbụ ibu and na-aga.
igbo_raw: Ibure ibulu ka mwady agwanwa nojekg gefe obodo (Ubul.).
english_raw: If you get trouble you carry it, as a man said to his son who was going out in the town. Warning to child.

igbo: Ọkụlọ adịghị asọ onye kọrọ ya.
english: Ọkụlọ does not grow bigger than the planter.
usage: Warning to child.
note: The final word is read as ya (the one who planted it); 'Work and idleness' appears to be a topic heading.
igbo_raw: Qkulo adesonari onye ko ani (Ubul.).
english_raw: Qkrg does not grow bigger than the planter. Warning to child. WorK AND IDLENEsS.

igbo: A kpọkọ ụlọ, a hụwa nkọ.
english: If they unroof a house, they see wood.
usage: If a man plants yams but does not weed, he gets no yams.
note: Thomas's 'uno' and 'afuwa' are normalized to standard ụlọ and a hụwa.
igbo_raw: AkbokB uno afuwa nko (I.A.).
english_raw: If they unroof a house, they see wood. If man plants yams, but does not weed, he gets no yams.

igbo: Otu isi anaghị ahụ ụzọ nri ụtụtụ; ọ dị ka ọbụ atala (akpịrị).
english: One head does not see the road to breakfast; it is like economising.
usage: When a man takes no one with him to farm.
note: The OCR is badly damaged; the reading follows the English sense and known proverb shape.
igbo_raw: Mby isi afur' yzQ bwazi; qdika obp atala (akbili) (Ala).
english_raw: One head does not see the road to breakfast; it is like economising. When a man takes no one with him to farm.

igbo: Ọkpa e ji aga ubi adịghị aka nwa ji.
english: A basket they take to farm never comes back without small yams.
note: Thomas's 'jogo' is read as e ji aga, and ubi is supplied from the sense.
igbo_raw: Okba jogo adabwa aka nwaji (0.0.).
english_raw: A basket they take to farm never comes back without small yams.

igbo: Mụ na ha jiri igwe, ọ dị ka anyị nọ n'otu.
english: I and they work together, it is as though we are all one.
usage: A solitary man who sees a crowd at work.
note: 'yili igwe' is uncertain; read as jiri igwe, though 'yiri igwe' (resemble iron) is also possible.
igbo_raw: Mu na wa yili igwe, odika ainya néa b'ofu (Ala).
english_raw: I and they work together, it is as though we are all one. A solitary man who sees a crowd at work.

igbo: Mmadụ adịghị akọ ntutu isi ya.
english: A man does not shave his own hair.
usage: When a man asks ebo to go with him to work and they cry off.
note: 'Mwady adako orwe' si' restored as Mmadụ adịghị akọ ntutu isi ya.
igbo_raw: Mwady adako orwe' si (0.0.).
english_raw: A man does not shave his own hair. When a man asks ebo to go with him to work and they cry off.

igbo: Akụ agwụghị, agba agaghị ezu ike.
english: If the kernels are not finished, the jaw will not rest.
usage: A man must finish his work.
note: Restored 'agwụghị' and 'agaghị ezu ike' from OCR 'aguna' and 'gezu'.
igbo_raw: Âkò aguna, abwa gezu ike (0.0.).
english_raw: If the kernels are not finished, the jaw will not rest. A man must finish his work.

igbo: Ọnwụ gburu onye na-egbu mmadụ; nke na-ele anya na-asị na ya ga-ata ọka ọtụmị.
english: Death kills one that sacrifices a person; one who looks on says he will live (bite corn) longer.
usage: By a man who gives up work.
note: OCR is badly corrupt; restored from the known proverb shape, with first word read as Ọnwụ (death).
igbo_raw: Qrwu çbug oji madu mese ; nke enes' ainya asi naiya
english_raw: gat' oka otpmi (0.0.). Death kills one that sacrifices person ; one who looks on says he will livo (bite corn) longer. By a man who gives up work.

igbo: Nkwụ daa, ọkà atọpụ.
english: Palm tree falls, younger one comes up.
usage: To encourage one who finds his work hard; all labour has an end.
note: 'tepu' read as atọpụ; 'bard' corrected to hard.
igbo_raw: Nkwadá oka tepu (0.0.).
english_raw: Palm tree falls, younger one comes up. To encourage one who finds his work bard; all labour has an end.

igbo: Ọ bụ ọbụwa jiri onwe ya n'anwụ.
english: Who hoes, stands in the sun.
usage: When a worker has not finished with his fellows.
note: 'obwa' read as ọbụwa (hoe); 'ji onwe' expanded to jiri onwe ya, but the proverb remains uncertain.
igbo_raw: Obu obwa ji onwe n' anwu (As.).
english_raw: Who hoes, stands in the sun. When a worker has not finished with his fellows.

igbo: Ife onye na-arụ bụ ubi ya.
english: What one does is his farm.
usage: Every one has his own work.
note: 'alo' read as na-arụ; 'ubwue' as ubi ya.
igbo_raw: Ife onye alo b'ubwue (0.0.).
english_raw: What one does is his farm. Every one has his own work.

igbo: Ogo na-ayo ọrụ, di na-ayo ọrụ.
english: Father-in-law asks for work, husband asks for work.
note: 'plu' and 'glu' read as ọrụ.
igbo_raw: Ogo aiyo plu di aiyo glu (Uk.).
english_raw: Father-in-law asks work, di asks work.

igbo: Ene na-eri ọkụrọ, ọ na-aga iburu ọgwụ ọkụrị.
english: Bush buck eats okro, goes to get medicine for dry cough.
usage: Workman must look to his tools.
note: 'meli' read as na-eri; 'ogunrhi' likely ọgwụ ọkụrị; 'buluje' as na-aga iburu.
igbo_raw: Ene meli pkulo, pne buluje ogunrhi (Uk.).
english_raw: Bush buck eat okro, goes to get medicine for dry cough. Workman must look to his tools.

igbo: Nwa gburu onye, nwa ka a ga-amụkwa.
english: A child kills one, a child they will bear.
usage: If a man is killed at work, others do the same work, e.g. climbing.
note: 'Bu' read as gburu; 'iwa' as nwa.
igbo_raw: Nwa Bu onye, iwa ka wagamukwa (Uk.).
english_raw: A child kills one, child (that) they will bear. If man is killed at work, others do same work, e.g., climbing.

igbo: Ịbara mkpu adịbeghị amamihe, ife uzu.
english: Those who run out at a shout are not the wiser ones.
usage: One who has work to do begins before helpers come.
note: 'ife uzg' uncertain; proverb only partly recoverable.
igbo_raw: Ibwarikpu adeby amwam' ife uzg (Uk.).
english_raw: Those who run out at a shout are not the wiser ones. One who has work to do begins before helpers come.

igbo: Ha adịghị ebu ebi aga ịgba afa n'ala.
english: They do not carry elephantiasis to divine on the ground.
usage: When a busy man is called for other work.
note: 'abw' af' alo' uncertain; restored as aga ịgba afa n'ala.
igbo_raw: Fadebu ibi abw' af' alo n'ani (Ubul.).
english_raw: They don't carry elephantiasis to divine on the ground. When busy man is called for other work.

igbo: Ọbọ butere mbibi na ntịkọ.
english: Laziness brings spoiling and destruction.
note: OCR damaged; the final word is uncertain, perhaps ntịkọ or ntịkụ.
igbo_raw: Obp bute mbibi na ntikpg (As.).
english_raw: Laziness brings spoiling and destruction.

igbo: Afọ jee, ka ọ bịa, adịghị efele n'ọnụ.
english: The year goes, let it come; it is not hard (scarce) to a lazy man in his mouth.
note: OCR 'nut' read as 'not'; the Igbo phrase after adịghị is uncertain.
igbo_raw: Arg je, k' pbia adiako efele n' omp (As.).
english_raw: The year goes, let it come; is nut hard (scarce) to a lazy man in his mouth.

igbo: Nkpụlọobi onye ọbọ na-achọ, ma o nweghị ihe.
english: The heart of a lazy man desires and has nothing.
note: OCR 'mwa' read as ma; nkpụlọobi is retained as a dialect form of heart.
igbo_raw: Nkpulobi onye obg nacg mwa odenw' ife (As.).
english_raw: The heart of a lazy man desires and has nothing.

igbo: Nke onye nwere, ibe enweghị; ijiji jị akwa, ngwele bụ ọtọ.
english: What one has, another has not; the fly has a cloth; the lizard is naked.
usage: A lazy man may prosper.
igbo_raw: Nk' onye nwe ibe enwerhye ijiji jäkwä ngwele by Qtg (Ala).
english_raw: What one has, another has not; the fly has a cloth; the lizard is naked. A lazy man may prosper.

igbo: Uzere enyere ụkwara aka.
english: Sneezing assists the cough.
usage: A lazy man makes excuses — I can't go to farm; there is work in the town.
note: OCR 'Uzele' read as uzere and 'okwala' as ụkwara.
igbo_raw: Uzele enyelu okwala aka (0.0.).
english_raw: Sneezing assists the cough. A lazy man makes excuses (I can't go to farm; there is work in the town).

igbo: Ubi tụrụ ime, ọ dị efele ka ọ weli.
english: The farm produces (conceives); it is the lazy man that takes them.
usage: Said to a lazy man.
note: OCR is garbled; ọ dị may stand for ọ bụ, and weli for were.
igbo_raw: Ubwo tul' ime qdi efele k' oweli (As.).
english_raw: The farm produces (conceives), it is the lazy man that takes them. To lazy man.

igbo: Udene adịghị eje ahịa ụra; udene zụta ihe, ọ na-ala.
english: The vulture does not go to market to sleep; the vulture buys and goes.
usage: Don't waste morning.
note: OCR 'aláro' read as ụra and 'eldle' as ala.
igbo_raw: Udene ádeje afia aláro; udene zd if' eldle, qná (Uk.).
english_raw: The vulture does not go to market to sleep; the vulture buys and goes. Don't waste morning.

igbo: Ilo si na nwata bọọ ije, ya bọọ ọlu.
english: The nightjar says that a boy runs after it; it stops him from working.
usage: If a boy plays instead of working in the farm, he gets still more work.
note: OCR 'Ilo' and the proverb's exact force remain somewhat uncertain.
igbo_raw: Ilo si na rwata boa ije, yaboa qlu (As.).
english_raw: Night jar says that boy runs after him, he stops him from working. If a boy plays instead of working in farm, he gets more work still.

igbo: Iyi adịghị eri mbabọ isi.
english: The river does not eat a blind calabash (i.e., an unbroken one).
note: OCR 'Lyi' and 'adéli' normalized; 'See 755' is a cross-reference.
igbo_raw: Lyi adéli mbabô isi (Ala).
english_raw: River does not eat blind calabash (¿.e., unbroken). See 755.

igbo: Nwata bụ enyi okenye, n'okwu erughị ya.
english: If a child is the friend of an old man, palaver does not meet him.
usage: But he must not trust to it; when palaver comes, he is forsaken.
note: OCR 'Bgsi' and 'ekulurhue' restored; the dialect word for friend may be 'ọsị'.
igbo_raw: Nwätä Bgsi ökêl; n'okwu ekulurhue (Ala).
english_raw: If a child is the friend of an old man, palaver does not meet him. (But he must not trust to it; when palaver comes, he is forsaken.)

igbo: Okopụ mwaka bụ eze ọrịa.
english: Downcast is king of illness.
usage: To cheer up in misfortune.
note: OCR 'plia' read as 'ọrịa'; 'mwaka' kept as transcribed.
igbo_raw: Okopum mwaka bi eze plia (Ubul.).
english_raw: Downcast is king of illness. To cheer up! in misfortune.

igbo: Otu nne dị iche.
english: One's own brother is different.
usage: A man standing alone is weak.
note: OCR 'diée' read as 'dị iche'.
igbo_raw: Ofu nne diée (0.0.).
english_raw: One's own brother is different. A man standing alone is weak.

igbo: Otu onye jee ije, ọdụdụ ata ya.
english: One man goes alone, tsetse kills him.
usage: There is safety in numbers.
note: OCR 'iyilu' and 'atabue' read as travel and bite formulae.
igbo_raw: Ofu onye iyilu, ódudù atabue (0.0.).
english_raw: One man goes alone, tsetse kills him. There is safety in numbers.

igbo: Ọba sị, nwụrụ ala onye ọwa fụnere ya n'ala Idụ.
english: The king says find for him one who is a failure in the land of Idú.
usage: One who sees another in need and tries to help.
note: The OCR leaves 'owa' and 'fienerhi' uncertain; the Igbo reading is tentative.
igbo_raw: Oba si nwurhala onye owa fienerhi n'ani Idú (Uk.).
english_raw: The king says find for him one who is a failure in the land of Idú. One who sees another in need and tries to help.

igbo: Ọsa bute, ọ bute n'ụze; ụze bute, ọ bute n'ọsa.
english: Osa fetches, fetches for Uze; Uze fetches for Osa (Osa and Uze are species of squirrels).
usage: Brothers help each other.
note: OCR 'фsá' read as 'ọsa'; 'l'' treated as dialectal 'n''.
igbo_raw: Osa bute, obute l' uze ; uze bute obute l' фsá (As.).
english_raw: Osa fetches, fetches for uze; uze fetches for osa. (Qsa and uze are species of squirrels.) Brothers help each other.

igbo: Alọlọ bụ ike ji; ji na-enweghị alọlọ agbaghị elu.
english: A small yam stick is the strength of the yam; without alolo it does not climb.
usage: Of a man who has no supporter.
note: OCR 'gmäinyi enu' read as 'agbaghị elu'.
igbo_raw: Alolo b' íkeji; ji afuna alolo gmäinyi enu (0.0.).
english_raw: A small yam stick is the strength of the yam; without alolo it does not climb. Of a man who has no supporter.

igbo: Ọ bụsi onye ji agụ igụ, anaghị efu n'ihi mwakọ na-egbu ihe bụ.
english: The day one takes to look for a louse, he does not lose because he looks for things that kill him.
usage: When a farmer hunts pig instead of working.
note: OCR is badly damaged; the Igbo is a tentative restoration and 'mwakọ' remains uncertain.
igbo_raw: Obgsi onye ji ¿g igu, anana n'iyi mwakan' geg ife Bu
english_raw: eni (I.A.). The day one takes to look for a louse, he does not lose because he looks for things that kill him. When a farmer hunts pig instead of working.

igbo: Nwata riri isi nnụnụ, ọ gaa uji.
english: A child eats the head of a bird, he goes to uji (hole in tree, where birds come for water, i.e., tries to shoot them).
usage: To an idle busybody who changes his ways.
note: OCR 'nnono' and 'gg' restored to nnụnụ and ọ gaa; 'uji' kept as Thomas's local term.
igbo_raw: Nwata lie'si nnono, gg'uji (0.0.).
english_raw: A child eats head of bird, he goes to uji (hole in tree, where birds come for water, ¿e., tries to shoot them). To idle busybody who changes his ways.

igbo: Aka arụ, ọ na-ọlị.
english: The hand tells when to leave work. Fatigue, not the hour, decides a man to stop.
note: 'arha' read as arụ and 'ong oly' as ọ na-ọlị; the verb 'ọlị' may be dialectal.
igbo_raw: Aka arha, ong oly (0.0.).
english_raw: The hand tells when to leave work. Fatigue, uot the hour, decides a man to stop.

igbo: Ọ dịla onye mma, gịnị k'ọ ga-egbu gaa be dibia?
english: If it is well with one, why does he go to the doctor's house?
note: The second half of the Igbo is uncertain; OCR 'k'gég kg' is not fully recoverable.
igbo_raw: Qdil' onye mma, gini k'gég kg be dibia (0.0.).
english_raw: If it is well with one, why does he go to the doctor's house?

igbo: Onye bu akpọnụ adaghị ebu ntọkẹ.
english: One who has goitre does not wear small beads (coral).
note: 'akbonu' and 'ntoke' read as akpọnụ and ntọkẹ.
igbo_raw: Onye bu akbonu ada ebwe ntoke (Uk.).
english_raw: Who has goitre does not wear small bead (coral).

igbo: Onye na-eje nwayọ na-agba ọsọ.
english: A quiet goer runs fast (i.e., does much harm).
usage: Of a quiet man.
note: OCR 'Anggon' ggon nabwaÿ' qsp' restored from the English; the exact verb form is uncertain.
igbo_raw: Anggon' ggon nabwaÿ' qsp (As.).
english_raw: A quiet goer runs fast (¿.e., does much harm). Of quiet man.

igbo: Ka onye si je, ka e bu ya.
english: As one's rank, so they give seat. As one's appearance, so they give seat.
note: '(si)' is optional in Thomas; 'bw¢la' read as bu ya.
igbo_raw: K' onye (si) je', ka wa bw¢la (0.0.).
english_raw: (a) As one's rank, so they give seat. (b) As one's appearance, so they give seat.

igbo: Omume onye bụ mma.
english: A man's deeds are his 'beauty.'
usage: When a girl refuses one man and chooses a worse-looking one.
note: OCR 'Àmal'' read as Omume and 'by' as bụ.
igbo_raw: Àmal' onye by mma (0.0.).
english_raw: A man's deeds are his " beauty." When a girl refuses one man and chooses a worse. looking one.

igbo: Anaghị anọ n'azụ ụlọ akọ ụlọ mma.
english: They never stay behind the house and say the house is good. Appearances are deceptive.
note: Restored Wadang as A naghị anọ and ajo as akọ; the negative form is uncertain.
igbo_raw: Wadang n'az' ung ajo ung mmwa (Ala).
english_raw: They never stay behind the house and say the house is good. Appearances are deceptive (?).

igbo: Ujuju adị aka mma n'isi anyịike, ma ọ mụwa, ọ taa.
english: The tree is very good for the head of the axe, but it will not last. Appearances are deceptive; chance acquaintance may be poor.
note: The final clause ma ọ mụwa, ọ taa is uncertain and may not carry Thomas's exact negative sense.
igbo_raw: Ujuju adçkamwa n'isi ainyike, mwomwa tè (0.0.).
english_raw: (Tree) is very good for the head of the axe, but it will not last. Appearances are deceptive; chance acquaintance may be poor.

igbo: A naghị eji isi awọ eke ubi.
english: They never take plots in farm by grey hair. A thin man may have a big farm.
note: Restored Âduwe as A naghị and en' ubwo as eke ubi.
igbo_raw: Âduwe eji isi awg en' ubwo (0.0.).
english_raw: They never take plots in farm by grey hair. A thin man may have a big farm. Cf. 451.

igbo: Kpakpa tụrụ ọkọ, nwa mara mma kọdị n'enu, ọ dana n'ani ịcha akpụ.
english: The cotton tree flower is fine when it is up, it falls as a nut. A young woman is fine, an old woman withered.
note: nwomalimwa and icelakg are uncertain; nwa mara mma may stand for a fuller phrase such as nwa agbọghọ mara mma.
igbo_raw: Kpakpa tulu ôkô nwomalimwa kodi nenu, odan' ani icelakg (As.).
english_raw: The cotton tree flower is fine when it is up, it falls (in) a nut. A young woman is fine, an old woman withered.

igbo: Ozugunzugu si na onye obụ ihe nkiti, n'anya adịghị n'onye fụ mma.
english: Owl says who kept silence; the eye of that one is not good.
usage: Wrongdoer injures man who says nothing; next time injured man threatens revenge.
note: OCR split fu mmwa across the Igbo and English lines; the proverb's exact ending remains uncertain.
igbo_raw: Ozugunzugu si'; n' onye obwaëinkiti n'ainya adin' onye
english_raw: fu mmwa (I.A.). Owl says who kept silence; the eye of that one is not good. Wrongdoer injures man who says nothing; next time injured man threatens revenge.

igbo: Onye anya mpi kwuru okwu mbụ, kwuru abụọ; asị ya, tụpị anya gị nọọ n'osọ.
english: Half blind man (blind of one eye) spoke once, spoke twice; they say to him: close your eyes and go aside.
usage: Injured man says this. If a man injures another twice without apology, he pays penalty.
note: topibate ainya nonosg is damaged; tụpị anya gị nọọ n'osọ is a probable but uncertain restoration.
igbo_raw: Onye ainya mpi kwu okwumbo kwu abg; asiya topibate
english_raw: ainya nonosg (O.0.). Half blind man (blind of one eye) spoke once, spoke twice ; they say to him: close your eyes and go aside. (Injured man says this). If a man injures another twice without apology, he pays penalty.

igbo: Ọfị adịghị egbu nwa, fanye ya afịa nne ya ịja afịa.
english: White yaws does not kill a child, they take it to flatter the mother.
usage: To console man in trouble.
note: Ofi oidá and fajte afia are damaged; the proverb's wording is not fully secure.
igbo_raw: Ofi oidá adebu iwa fajte afia nneriwa afia (Ala).
english_raw: White yaws does not kill a child, they take it to flatter the mother. To console man in trouble.

igbo: Ije a dị; ka m kee kwu zi?
english: (Let) the journey (be) so; what am I to say?
usage: When a man comes from court and says he has been heavily fined.
note: k'ike ege kwuzi read as ka m kee kwu zi.
igbo_raw: Ijei adi; k'ike ege kwuzi? (0.0.).
english_raw: (Let) the journey (be) so; what am I to say ? When a man comes from court and says he has been heavily fined.

igbo: Oti akị ti akị, nke bu ọkịele abịa n'ọbụ.
english: Who breaks nut, breaks nut, who gathers shells has fame.
usage: Refusing to do another man's work.
note: OCR 'aky/akq' read as akị; 'iõele' as ọkịele; final 'nal' oup' as n'ọbụ.
igbo_raw: Oti aky ti akq, nke bu iõele abia nal' oup (Ubul.).
english_raw: Who breaks nut, breaks nut, who gathers shells has fame. Refusing to do another man's work.

igbo: Anụ na-amụgharị anaghị abanye n'ọnya.
english: An animal that trembles does not walk into a trap.
usage: One who works becomes rich.
note: Thomas's 'nonana' may be 'anaghị anọ'; normalized to abanye on the English.
igbo_raw: Anp any nni amwaya nonana n' oinya (Ubul.).
english_raw: An animal that trembles does not walk into a trap. One who works becomes rich

igbo: Ọkịkọ bụ ọrụ, ịkwa bụ ọrụ. Ọrụ bụ ọrụ.
english: Tying the sticks on the roof is work, patching is work; work is work.
note: Normalized Asaba ọlu/oly to standard ọrụ; 'Okike' read as ọkịkọ.
igbo_raw: Okike by olu, pwa bu oly (As.).
english_raw: Tying the sticks (on the roof) is work, patching is work. Work is work.

igbo: Ha ziri ọkà bịa gbaa; ọ sị na ya amaghị agba.
english: They send to the hunter to come and shoot; he says he does not know how.
usage: When a man sent for to do work cannot do it.
note: Wadasi read as ha ziri; 'abwa' as agba; 'amwasina' as amaghị.
igbo_raw: Wadasi çkà bia abwa; qsi naiya amwasina abwa (0.0.).
english_raw: They send to the hunter to come and shoot; he says he does not know how. When a man sent for to do work cannot do it.

igbo: Azịza abụghị ihe; n'ụtụtụ ha na-achọ azịza, ọ dịghị.
english: A broom is nothing; in the morning they go about looking for a broom.
usage: When a worker is sent for after a man has said he is worthless.
note: Final 'ojnili' read as ọ dịghị; English omits it.
igbo_raw: Aziza abur' ife; otôto wa¢o aziza ojnili (Ala).
english_raw: A broom is nothing; in the morning they go about looking for a broom. When a worker is sent for after man has said he is worthless.

igbo: Amasị ịwata ọkụ, dọseni ọkọ, ọ sị na agụ na-agụ ya.
english: They don't say to a child 'make fire'; and he says he is hungry.
usage: A man does not provide food till work is done.
note: Wamosi read as Amasị; 'qkq' as ọkọ; 'nagu naguya' as na-agụ na-agụ ya.
igbo_raw: Wamosi iwata ; duseni qkq ; qsi nagu naguya (Ala).
english_raw: They don't say to a child "make fire"; and he says he is hungry. A man does not provide food till work is done.

igbo: Ha eli, afọ ọ pụta.
english: When they eat, the belly comes out.
usage: A man calls people to work, and feeds them; then they work.
note: Weli read as ha eli; 'Üpità' as ọ pụta.
igbo_raw: Weli, afg Üpità (0.0.).
english_raw: When they eat, the belly comes out. A man calls people to work, and feeds them; then they work.

igbo: Ha adịghị eji afọ ọkọ ata ụfọlị.
english: They never take spice with empty belly.
usage: If someone asks a man to work without preparing food.
note: Wadeji read as ha adịghị eji; 'alö da'' likely ọkọ ata; OCR badly garbled.
igbo_raw: Wadeji afo ufoly alö da' (0.0.).
english_raw: They never take spice with empty belly. If someone asks a man to work without preparing food.

igbo: Nwata gbue ọlọbwe; ọ hụghị ọkụ o ji ria ya.
english: A child kills a boa; it does not see fire to roast it.
usage: When a man can't find a helper.
note: The boa term and OCR damage make the opening words uncertain; restored from the sense.
igbo_raw: Nwata Bue plolobwe; odafu pko oji arhya (Uk.).
english_raw: A child kills a boa; it does not see fire to roast it. When a man can't find a helper.

igbo: Osoko je be Ogwoko.
english: Osoko goes to Ogwoko (helpless runs to helpless).
usage: When a man with a palaver gets a useless backer.
note: OCR 'Osokg' and 'Ogwpkq' restored to Osoko and Ogwoko.
igbo_raw: Osokg jè be Ogwpkq (As.).
english_raw: Osoko goes to Ogwoko (helpless runs to helpless). When a man with palaver gets useless backer.

igbo: Àdàkada sị n'ugwu: Ọ kụkụ ka ị na-akwụ ibu, ka ị na-ebu? Ọ na-ana ya, ka ị na-ana ya?
english: The dung beetle says to the hill: are you helping him with his load or do you take it from him?
usage: To a false friend in a palaver.
note: The middle of the proverb is badly garbled; the reading is provisional.
igbo_raw: Adàkada si énugu : Ökükwg k'inakwua ibug k'pbu qnena k'inanaiya (As.).
english_raw: The dung beetle says to the hill: are you helping him with his load or do you take it from bim ? To a false friend in palaver.

igbo: Ka anyị na-ele ụwa.
english: Look at the world.
usage: Consolation for misfortune.
note: OCR 'nene owa' restored to na-ele ụwa.
igbo_raw: Ka nene owa (As.).
english_raw: Look at the world. Consolation for misfortune.

igbo: A kụrụ akpụ maka ụnwụ; ụnwụ anwụ, akpụ a bịa.
english: They plant pumpkin for a famine; the famine goes, pumpkin begins to bear.
usage: If the trusted helper fails.
note: The stray 'meva' is unresolved and the Igbo is reconstructed from damaged OCR.
igbo_raw: Ak'obwggulu mwak' onwu; onwu aná, obwogulu abia
english_raw: meva (0.0.). They plant pumpkin for a famine; the famine goes, pumpkin begins to bear. If the trusted helper fails.

igbo: Ọ bụrụ na mmiri taa, ọ na-eru n'obi.
english: Even if the river dries much it reaches (catches) the chest.
usage: Consolation; "you have suffered all and cannot suffer more."
note: OCR 'Orhimili taka' restored to Ọ bụrụ na mmiri taa.
igbo_raw: Orhimili taka obe n'obi (0.0.).
english_raw: Even if the river dries much it reaches (catches) the chest. Consolation; "you have suffered all and cannot suffer more."

igbo: Onye mere ya, ya dị ya.
english: Let him bear it, to whom it happens.
usage: To a man who laments his losses (he must bear up).
note: OCR 'yadi be' restored to ya dị ya.
igbo_raw: Onye ome yadi be (Ala).
english_raw: Let him bear it, to whom it happens. To man who laments his losses (he must bear up).

igbo: Ọ bụrụ na ụnwụ akawaa, anyasị ka ụnwụ ji ala.
english: However big the famine, in the evening famine takes a small yam.
usage: Even after big losses we eat.
note: The OCR is badly damaged; the reading is uncertain.
igbo_raw: Orwu mwakada, ainyase k' onwu ji alg (Ubul.).
english_raw: However big the famine, in the evening famine takes a small yаm. Even after big losses we eat.

igbo: Ọnwụ agụka na-akọ anyasị
english: Famine satisfaction comes in the evening (to a hungry child).
note: The Igbo is badly damaged in the OCR and Thomas's transcription; 'See 541' is a cross-reference, not usage.
igbo_raw: Onwu algka nako ainyase (0.0.).
english_raw: Famine satisfaction comes in the evening (to hungry child). See 541.

igbo: A sị m bụrụ nwoke, m ga-eso gị abụọ
english: If I had been a man, I would have made you two (i.e. accompanied you).
usage: Sister to brotherless man.
note: Thomas's dialect transcription is damaged, so the proverb is restored to its standard known form.
igbo_raw: Bura n'atamb'okei, nta melimi ouy' abo (Ala).
english_raw: If I had been a man, I would have made you two (i.e. accompanied yon). Sister to brotherless man.

igbo: Chi mmadụ dị abụọ
english: A man's chi are two.
usage: A doctor is like a man's chi; said if a man saves a boy from a big man.
note: 'Ci' is normalized to chi.
igbo_raw: Ci mwado di aboa (Ala).
english_raw: A man's ci are two. (A doctor is like a man's Ci.) If man saves boy from big man.

igbo: Abụzị na-akwa n'ikpere anyasị, ọ na-abanye n'ime olulu, ọ maghị na chi agwụla
english: A cricket cries, in the evening it goes into a hole, it does not know that the night is far gone.
usage: A prudent man lays up for a rainy day.
note: Several words in Thomas's transcription are uncertain, especially the final clause.
igbo_raw: Abuzy Aja n'ikbele ainyase daba n'ime onp omwarpzi na ¿i no n'ogudu (Ala).
english_raw: A cricket cries, in the evening it goes into a hole, does not know that the night is far gone. A prudent man laya up for a rainy day.

igbo: A sị m ma adịghị ebute ụzọ, n'azụ ka ọ na-abịa
english: "If I had known" does not come first but last; prudence comes after the event.
note: The first word is OCR-garbled in Thomas, but the proverb is well known.
igbo_raw: Mwalibo adeb uzg, n'azq k'onakbe (Ala).
english_raw: " If I had known" does not come first but last. Prudence comes after the event. с 2

igbo: Nwata amaghị ụwa, ọ na-aja ji n'ọmẹ
english: A child does not know the world, he praises a yam in shoots (half-grown).
usage: Examine before you praise.
igbo_raw: Nwata amwarg uwe, onaja ji n'ome (Ala).
english_raw: A child does not know the world, he praises a yam in shoots (half-grown). Examine before you praise.

igbo: Ajọ nrọ adịghị eketu mmadụ n'ụlọ mụọ
english: A bad dream never leaves a man in the house of the mụọ.
usage: By a man who retires from matter to avoid ill consequences.
note: The verb 'eketu' and the reading of 'mụọ' are uncertain in the damaged OCR.
igbo_raw: Ajonlgadeketg mwadu be mwg (Ubul.).
english_raw: A bad dream never leaves a man in house of the mwo. By a man who retires from matter to avoid ill consequences.

igbo: Adịghị asa nke ọma karịa onye jere iyi
english: They never wash better than the one who went to the river.
usage: If a cook complains of not getting enough food.
note: OCR makes 'karịa' and 'iyi' uncertain.
igbo_raw: Adawy nari onye jiyi arhy (0.0.).
english_raw: They never wash better than the one who went to the river. If cook complains of not getting enough food.

igbo: Onye ngwụrọ na-arịọ ibe ji abụọ ka o ru aka
english: Lame man asks for two slices of yam that one may reach him.
usage: When a man begs for more than he wants to make sure of getting something.
note: OCR is severely garbled; reconstructed from the English and the known proverb.
igbo_raw: Qkumn ku ibeji nabp kofu lu aka (As.).
english_raw: Lame man asks for two slices of yam that one may reach him. When a man begs for more than he wants to make sure of getting something.

igbo: Ilolo bụ ike
english: Taking thought is strength.
usage: To a man who has hard work to live.
igbo_raw: Ilolo bu ike (0.0.).
english_raw: Taking thought is strength. To a man who has hard work to live.

igbo: Ije k'obi ọ ma ihe ọ ga-agwa obi; ọ mazị ihe obi ga-agwa ya
english: Who goes to obi knows the thing he will say to obi; he does not know what obi will say to him when he goes to him.
usage: When a man gets farm land, they say 'take plenty'; he does not, and finds the land is good.
note: Last phrase in OCR ('mw'qu akg') is uncertain; restored from the known proverb as 'ihe obi ga-agwa ya'.
igbo_raw: Fjek'öbi omwai ife oga gwobi; omazi nk'obi gagwa
english_raw: mw'qu akg (I.A.). Who goes to obi knows the thing he will say to obi; he does not know what obi will say to him when he goes to him. When a man gets farm land, they say "take plenty"; he does not and finds the land is good.

igbo: Anwụ lamalama na-eli ji
english: The sun shines a little and eats yams; a stitch in time saves nine.
igbo_raw: Anwu lamalama neli ji (I.A.).
english_raw: The sun shines a little and eats yams. A stitch in time saves nine.

igbo: Onye gbúrú agụ zị onwe ya Idu
english: One who kills a leopard sends himself to Idu (the leopard was formerly sent to Oba Idu); a thief counts his punishment.
note: OCR 'awolo' is uncertain; read as agụ (leopard) from the English note.
igbo_raw: Onye Bu' awolo zi onwe Idt (0.0.).
english_raw: One who kills a leopard sends himself to Idu. (Leopard was formerly sent to Oba Idu.) A thief counts his punishment.

igbo: Mmadụ amaghị ebe ọ ga-ata ọjị
english: A man does not know how long he has to live.
usage: If a man refuses to plant kola, he thinks he will not eat of it.
note: OCR 'atadebo' read as 'ata ọjị' (chew kola); Thomas's English is a loose paraphrase.
igbo_raw: Mwad' amwana eb' ojekg atadebo (0.0.).
english_raw: A man does not koow how long he has to live. If a man refuses to plant kola, thinks he will not eat of it.

igbo: Inyi adịghị egbu ọgwụ egbu onye so ya
english: Inyi tree does not kill witch and kill who accompanies him.
usage: By a man who retires from a matter to avoid ill consequences.
note: OCR is damaged; 'obwome' read as ọgwụ and 'dugeni' as so ya, but both are uncertain.
igbo_raw: Inyi adebu obwome eBu onye dugeni (Ubul.).
english_raw: Inyi tree does not kill witch and kill who accompanies him. By man who retires from matter to avoid ill consequences.

igbo: Ọnya adị anwụ agwọ
english: A trap does not catch a snake.
usage: If a person escapes his enemies.
note: Thomas's 'adi' may stand for adịghị; kept as transcribed.
igbo_raw: Oinya adi anwu agwg (As.).
english_raw: A trap does not catch a snake. If a person escapes his enemies.

igbo: A naghị agwa nwa ozu na ọ naghị eli ozu nke ọma, maka na ọ bụ nke mbụ.
english: They don't tell a child of a dead man that he does not bury well, because it is the first burial.
note: Restored from Thomas's damaged Asaba transcription; the negative and 'eli ozu' are inferred from the English.
igbo_raw: Wádosi rwa' ozu n'oning ofuma, mwakana onini mby (Uk.).
english_raw: They don't tell child of dead man that he does not bury well, because it is the first burial.

igbo: Ngwele elu da n'ani, sị madụ adịghị eja ya, ya jaa onwe ya.
english: A lizard falls down from above; it says people do not praise it, it praises itself.
usage: When work is well done and is not praised by the recipient.
note: Thomas's 'mwady' is restored as madụ and 'dikajaiya' as adịghị eja ya.
igbo_raw: Ngwele enu da n'ani, si mwady dikajaiya kaiya ja onweya (Ala).
english_raw: A lizard falls down from above, he says men don't praise him, he praises himself. When work is well done, and is not praised by recipient..

igbo: Oke bụ igwe n'ebo.
english: The old (big) man is the benefactor of the ebo.
usage: An ebo is badly off without a wise man.
note: The key word 'igg' is uncertain; 'igwe' is a guess from the English and Thomas's spelling.
igbo_raw: Okei b' igg n'ebo (Ala).
english_raw: The old (big) man is the benefactor of the ebo. An ebo is badly off' without a wise man.

igbo: Ụzọ dị jụụ, nduru ebu opi.
english: If the road is quiet, a dove blows a long flute.
usage: When a man asks advice, he waits till the councillor is disengaged.
note: Restored 'nduru' from 'nduli' and 'jụụ' from the English.
igbo_raw: Vzg d'owe nduli ebu opi (I.A.).
english_raw: If the road is quiet, a dove blows a long flute. When a man asks advice, he waits till councillor is disengaged.

igbo: Madụ alala nne.
english: If someone advises a man to wash his sore harder.
note: The English does not match the short Igbo and may itself be a garbled usage note; the proverb is kept as read.
igbo_raw: Mwady alalänne (0.0.).
english_raw: If someone advises a man to wash his sore harder.

igbo: Ike gwụrụ, ọnwụ bịa, esizi ike.
english: The fighter stops fighting when death comes.
usage: When a strong man commits murder and is hanged (he has been warned in these terms).
note: Restored 'gwụrụ' and 'ọnwụ' from Thomas's 'yalu' and 'prwu'.
igbo_raw: Ike yalu prwu yabia esizine (Ala).
english_raw: Fighter stops, when death comes, fighting. When a strong man commits murder, and is hung (he has been warned in these terms).

igbo: Kube ofe sie.
english: Take soup and boil.
usage: A strong man kills people; they use this proverb to advise him to stop.
note: Thomas's 'tie' is normalized to standard 'sie'; 'Kube' may be kụbe.
igbo_raw: Kubel' ofe tie (As.).
english_raw: Take soup and boil. A strong man kills people; they use this proverb to advise him to stop.

igbo: Onye kpọrọ ọnya, ọ na-ahịa ji.
english: One who has set a trap roasts yams and eats.
usage: Warning to a man who sleeps away from home without reason (e.g., goes visiting in town).
note: Restored 'kpọrọ ọnya' and 'ọ na-ahịa ji'; the final 'and eats' may represent an omitted eri.
igbo_raw: Onye kpobei oinya, orhplie ji (0.0.).
english_raw: One who has set a trap roasts yams and eats. Warning to a man who sleeps away from home without reason (e.g., goes visiting in town).

igbo: Arụrụ na-eso ogwe gafee iyi.
english: Insects follow a log to cross a river.
usage: A man takes a guide to unknown places.
note: Restored 'Arụrụ' (insects) and 'gafee' (cross) from Thomas's phonetic spelling.
igbo_raw: Arhôrhò nçso ógwè efe iyi (Ala).
english_raw: Insects follow a log to cross a river. A man takes a guide to unknown places.

igbo: Onye Ọka sị n'anya, ma jị mba, na ọ lụọ Ọka.
english: The craftsman who does favours gets no money.
note: OCR badly damaged; 'reach Awka' in Thomas's English is a literal fragment, not a usage note.
igbo_raw: Onye Oka si naiya ma ji mbana welu Oka (As.).
english_raw: reach Awka. Craftsman who does favours gets no money.

igbo: Ọmọtụ gbọọ anya.
english: A strong child that has no sense.
usage: To a violent man, or foolish.
note: OCR leaves the proverb uncertain; '(?Esa)' may be a place or a misread word.
igbo_raw: Qmotu gmoinya (?Esa) (0.0.).
english_raw: A strong child that has no sense. To a violent man, or foolish.

igbo: Ọ rọọ nrọ kwụ n'ụlọ, edina nrọ n'ụlọ.
english: Standing dreamt, lying down dreamt.
usage: It is no use losing one's temper because a thing is not done, if one has not taken thought before.
note: Restored 'nrọ' (dream) and 'n'ụlọ' (in the house) from OCR.
igbo_raw: Ada kwu gto algnlo, edineni alonlo (I.A.).
english_raw: Standing dreamt, lying down dreamt. It is no use losing one's temper because a thing is not done, if one has not taken thought before.

igbo: Onye jekwuru akwa, ya laa anya, ọ ga-eji gịnị akwa?
english: If a man who is going to cry loses his eyes, what will he cry with?
usage: If a person does not prepare.
note: Restored 'gịnị' (what) from OCR 'gekwa'.
igbo_raw: Onye jek' ákwá yal'ainya, ogeji gekwa (As.).
english_raw: If a man who is going to cry loses his eyes, what will he cry with? If a person does not prepare.

igbo: Ọ bụrụ na anyị aga n'ubi iri nri, anyị ga-ewe anwụrụ.
english: If we had gone to the farm to eat we should take smoke.
usage: If a person does not prepare.
note: OCR leaves the middle of the proverb uncertain; reading follows Thomas's English.
igbo_raw: Obuly ubwo agel' ife mwa nta anwul anwya (As.).
english_raw: If we had gone to the farm to eat we should take smoke. If a person does not prepare.

igbo: Ụbọchị erubeghị, a naghị akọ ya ọjọọ.
english: Day not done, they don't say it is not good (or bad).
note: OCR badly damaged; restored from the sense and Onitsha dialect 'ubosi'.
igbo_raw: Oi ejing, anakalo obosi (0.0.).
english_raw: Day not done, they don't say it is not good (or bad).

igbo: Anyị amaghị okwu, anyị atụ isi tinye.
english: We will not help one to speak and lose our heads.
note: OCR leaves the verb forms uncertain; reading is provisional.
igbo_raw: Ainyi amakg okg ba tu isi tinye (Ubul.).
english_raw: We will not help one to speak and lose our heads.

igbo: Ịta bụ nri ntị.
english: Tales are the food of the ear.
usage: To persuade an unwilling person to come.
note: Restored ntị from OCR rti and nri from nni.
igbo_raw: Ita bu nni rti (As.).
english_raw: Tales are the food of the ear. To persuade unwilling person to come.

igbo: Ọmata kwuru onye ọnụ, mbịa ya erighị.
english: If a good man meets a talkative one, his coming is useless.
usage: Of a man who traduces.
note: Restored ọnụ from ony; mbịa ya erighị is uncertain from OCR gtierhi.
igbo_raw: Qmata kwulu onye ony, mbia gtierhi (Ala).
english_raw: If a good man meets a talkative one, his coming is useless. Of a man who traduces.

igbo: Ọ bụ n'Ezomo onye ga-ebu Ọdịa?
english: If not Ezomo, who would have borne Odia.
usage: To a man who complains that Onirhe has done something to him.
note: OCR akamy restored as ga-ebu; Onirhe spelling uncertain.
igbo_raw: Obun' Ezqmg ony' akamy Qdia (0.0.).
english_raw: If not Ezomo, who would have borne Odia. To a man who complains that Onirhe has done something to him.

igbo: Elu na-eche.
english: The world thinks.
usage: When a man abuses another in the presence of others.
note: OCR Enu log restored as Elu na-eche; the reading remains uncertain.
igbo_raw: Enu log (0.0.).
english_raw: The world thinks, When a man abuses another in the presence of others.

igbo: Okwu n'azụ onye ya pụta ihu m, kwuo.
english: Let a backbiter come to my face and speak.
note: Restored n'azụ, pụta, ihu m, and kwuo from damaged OCR.
igbo_raw: Okwu n'azy onye yaputa irhum gekug.
english_raw: Let a backbiter come to my face and speak.

igbo: Efi nwere nne bụ obolo.
english: A cow that has a mother is a heifer (not old).
usage: When someone abuses one older than himself.
note: Restored nwere nne from inwgnne; corrected hinself to himself.
igbo_raw: Efi inwgnne by obwölo (As.).
english_raw: A cow that has a mother is a heifer (not old). When someone abuses one older than hinself.

igbo: Nnọkọ ọnụ na-ebute ọkà.
english: Sitting together causes backbiting.
usage: If a newcomer joins a party and tells lies in order to join them.
note: OCR is badly damaged; restored Nnọkọ ọnụ and ọkà from the English sense.
igbo_raw: Nng kgma burhe öká' (0.0.).
english_raw: Sitting together causes backbiting. If a newcomer joins party and tells lies in order to join them.

igbo: Ọ na-atamụ ka ogbome.
english: He speaks ill like a wizard (who is on bad terms with all).
note: OCR Onatamp and ogbome leave the proverb partly unrecoverable; the reading is tentative.
igbo_raw: Onatamp K' ogbome (As.).
english_raw: He speaks ill like a wizard (who is on bad terms with all).

igbo: Nkụjị mị ya ka abụọ ji kuru obogulu na ubi.
english: Leading out (bears it) makes calabash take pumpkin to the farm.
usage: When a man forgets his benefactor through selfishness; anger.
note: OCR 'm§' read as mị; 'obwogulu' and 'kulu' restored as obogulu/kuru.
igbo_raw: Nkuje m§ ya ka abwo ji kulu obwogulu na ubwo (0.0.).
english_raw: Leading out (bears it) makes calabash take pumpkin to the farm. When man forgets his benefactor through selfishness. AnGER.

igbo: Ifejioku adịghị egbu dị n'ubi, ma ọ na-aga.
english: Ifejioku does not kill the farmer in his farm, because he goes (to other farm).
usage: When a man says too much he lies.
note: OCR 'difi' and 'onakg' leave the proverb partly uncertain.
igbo_raw: Ifejioko ádebu difi n' ubwo, mw'onakg (Uk.).
english_raw: Ifejioko does not kill the farmer in his farm, because he goes (to other farm). When a man says too much he lies.

igbo: Ha adịghị eji iwe egbu nwa mma.
english: They don't take vexation to kill small knife.
note: OCR 'iketi akbubu' read as eji iwe egbu.
igbo_raw: Wadeji iketi akbubu nwamwa (Ubul.).
english_raw: They don't take vexation to kill small knife.

igbo: Iwe na-akpọ nwa ọfụ kee akwa; ebe ọfụ adịghị eji akwa n'ọhịa.
