english: Anger leads "fox" to tie cloth; the country of "fox" does not wear cloth in the bush.
usage: When a man acts in anger.
note: OCR 'je okg' and 'oko' restored as kee akwa and akwa.
igbo_raw: Iwe rha nwa ufu je okg; ebo ufu adeje oko n'ofia (Ubul.).
english_raw: Anger leads "fox" to tie cloth; the country of "fox" does not wear cloth in the bush. When a man acts in anger.

igbo: Nwata rie ife gbawara afọ, o were afọ buru uzọ.
english: If a child eats something that bursts belly, he puts belly before him.
usage: A man who causes trouble must bear it.
note: OCR 'bwepp' read as gbawara; 'owel'' as o were.
igbo_raw: Nwata lie ife bwepp afg, owel' afg bul uzg (0.0.).
english_raw: If a child eats something that bursts belly, he puts belly before him. A man who causes trouble must bear it.

igbo: Ife onye kọrọ, ọ kwọrọ ya.
english: What one sows, he reaps (bear for him).
note: OCR 'amila (kwomila)' leaves the second half uncertain.
igbo_raw: Ife onye ko, amila (kwomila) (0.0.).
english_raw: What one sows, he reaps (bear for him).

igbo: Ọnwụ egbughị iwokete, ọ mesịa ọ bụrụ ka nne nkwụ.
english: If death does not kill a young palm, afterwards it becomes a big palm.
usage: If a big boy beats a small boy; he can pay out later.
note: 'iwokete' and OCR 'olug' are uncertain; usage 'bog' read as boy.
igbo_raw: Onw' ebung iwokete omesie olug ka nnenku (0.0.).
english_raw: If death does not kill a young palm, afterwards it becomes a big palm. If a big boy beats a small bog; he can pay out later.

igbo: Nta wemere gọọ ife awobi; ma ọ bụna o ruo ụlọ, ọ gwa nwanne.
english: They would have treated a worthless man foolishly, but if he reaches home, he tells his brothers.
usage: A man takes money from his son-in-law; the son-in-law will get money for his daughters.
note: Line is split by OCR; 'Nta wemere gọọ ife awobi' remains uncertain.
igbo_raw: Nta weme gzoa ife awobi; n' obuna olu ung ogwa
english_raw: nwanne (0.0.). They would have treated a worthless man foolishly, but if he reaches home, he tells his brothers. A man takes money from his son-in-law; the son-in-law will get money for his daughters.

igbo: Onye asị na-ege ntị ire jọ, ọ bụ onye.
english: A liar listens to a bad tongue.
note: bw' onye read as bụ onye; the final clause is uncertain.
igbo_raw: Onye asi negenti ile jo bw' onye (As.).
english_raw: A liar listens to a bad tongue.

igbo: Ọkụkọ rịta ibe ji abụọ na-akwa akwa na ọ dịghị ya eze; ewu nwere eze, olee izi ọ na-eri?
english: A fowl eats two slices of yam and complains he has no teeth; a goat that has teeth, how many does it eat?
usage: Don't look a gift horse in the mouth.
note: elte read as rịta, iy'oya eze as na ọ dịghị ya eze, and ilizi one as olee izi ọ na-eri; these are uncertain.
igbo_raw: Qkoko elte ibeji nabo n'akw'akwa iy'oya eze ; ewu tw'eze ilizi one ? (Ala).
english_raw: A fowl eats two slices of yam and complains he has no teeth; a goat that has teeth, how many does it eat ? Don't look a gift horse in the mouth

igbo: E were ododo kpaa abọ, abọ ka ọ bụ.
english: They take a red cloth to make a long basket and it is a basket still.
usage: It is waste to do a kindness to the ungrateful.
note: Awelu read as E were; abọ kept as basket.
igbo_raw: Awelu ododo kpabo, abo k'obu (Ubul.).
english_raw: They take a red cloth to make a long basket and it's a basket still. It is waste to do a kindness to the ungrateful.

igbo: Nwata kweere ọrụ, nke ya na-eche ya.
english: A child agrees to work, his own waits for him.
usage: A kind-hearted person reaps ingratitude.
note: oly read as ọrụ; akwoly néce read as nke ya na-eche ya.
igbo_raw: Nwata kweke oly, nke akwoly néce (Ala).
english_raw: A child agrees to work, his own waits for him. A kind-hearted person reaps ingratitude.

igbo: Ebu m, ọnya m ebu; nke m gburu ekweghị m ịhụ nkpụ.
english: I kill, my trap kills; what I kill does not allow me to see my catch.
usage: When a man is ungrateful for father's help.
note: nkemBulu read as nke m gburu; gkwery gabwali пkpú as ekweghị m ịhụ nkpụ.
igbo_raw: Ebuem oinyam ebue; nkemBulu gkwery gabwali пkpú (As.).
english_raw: I kill, my trap kills; what I kill does not allow me to see my catch. When a man is ungrateful for father's help.

igbo: Onye mere ọgaranya, ọ na-echefu onye na-eche ya mgbe ọ bụ ogbenye.
english: When one becomes rich, he forgets one that keeps to him when he was poor.
usage: Ingratitude.
note: OCR badly damaged; reconstruction from English is probable but not certain.
igbo_raw: Onye me pdafi, pzo onye aneya ime ikpa (0.0.).
english_raw: When one becomes rich, he forgets one that keeps (to) him when he was poor. Ingratitude.

igbo: Atụ aka, aka mụọ ihe; atụ aka ọ bọdị, ọ fụọ aka.
english: If a man who receives help is ungrateful, he gets no help again.
note: OCR damaged; Thomas cross-refers to No. 918, omitted here.
igbo_raw: Atp aly pka, pka mwal ife; atu al' obodi, ofeji aka (O.0.).
english_raw: (Cf. No. 918.) If man who receives help is ungrateful, he gets no help again.

igbo: Ọkụkọ adịghị echefu onye dọpụrụ ọdụ ya n'oge udu mmiri.
english: A fowl does not forget who pulls out his tail in a rainy season.
usage: Gratitude.
note: adazg read as adịghị echefu; rh'odo as dọpụrụ ọdụ.
igbo_raw: Okoko adazg onye rh'odo udumili (0.0.).
english_raw: A fowl does not forget who pulls out his tail in a rainy season Gratitude.

igbo: Akwụkwọ asọsọ na-alụfụ nwa ewu
english: A sweet leaf deceives a kid; a thief is caught sooner or later.
note: Thomas's 'Akukwg' read as standard 'Akwụkwọ'; 'alụfy' expanded to 'na-alụfụ'.
igbo_raw: Akukwg asosg alçfy nwa' ewu (0.0.).
english_raw: A sweet leaf deceives a kid. A thief is caught sooner or later.

igbo: Onye tụba n'ala, ọ tụba n'elu
english: Who has much to do, has much to eat.
note: 'tụba' and 'n'elu' read from Thomas's Asaba forms; the sense is proverbial.
igbo_raw: Onye tuba naly ptuba neli (As.).
english_raw: Who has much to do, has much to eat.

igbo: Ụbụ ka n'ubu akpa, ma nkpo ka a na-akwụ
english: We carry a bag on the shoulder but it is hung on a peg; a carrier must have rest.
usage: Excuses and statements.
note: OCR 'n'ainy'' restored as 'n'ubu'; 'kobe' as 'akwụ'.
igbo_raw: Ubú ka n'ainy' akpa, mwa nkpo ka ne kobe (As.).
english_raw: We carry a bag on the shoulder but it is hung on a peg. A carrier must have rest. ExcUses aND STATEMENTS.

igbo: Ọ jụm, m nwebe ebe m na-eri
english: He is (I am) satisfied to have where he trusts that he stays to eat.
usage: Of a man who is annoyed and refuses to eat (he has somewhere to eat).
note: OCR badly damaged; reconstruction follows the known proverb about refusing food.
igbo_raw: Ojum rwebe deokume ong geli (0.0.).
english_raw: He is (I am) satisfied to have where he trusts that he stays to eat. Of a man who is annoyed and refuses to eat (he has some- where to eat).

igbo: Ọkwa ọrụ gbaa, ha zaa ya
english: A trumpeter calls for work, they answer him.
usage: When a man excuses himself by saying he did not hear.
note: 'wa' read as 'ọrụ' (work) and 'wazaiya' as 'ha zaa ya'.
igbo_raw: Qkwa wa gly, wazaiya (0.0.).
english_raw: A trumpeter calls for work, they answer him. When a man excuses himself by saying he did not hear.

igbo: Anụ m Nwambọ, amaghị m Nwambọ nke onye
english: I heard of Nwambo, I don't know whose Nwambo it is.
usage: By a witness who has nothing to say.
note: 'Nwambg' standardised as 'Nwambọ'; 'pby' as 'onye'.
igbo_raw: Anum Nwambg, Nwambg, amwanam Nwambg nk' pby (Ubul.).
english_raw: I heard of Nwambo, I don't know whose Nwambo it is. By a witness who has nothing to say.

igbo: Mmadụ adaghị onwe ya
english: A person does not deny himself.
usage: A man who fails is still the same man; he must not get a rich man to father him, and deny the name his father gave him.
note: OCR 'onw@' read as 'onwe ya'.
igbo_raw: Mwady adaju onw@ (Ala).
english_raw: A person does not deny himself. A man who fails is still the same man; he must not get a rich man to father him, and deny the name his father gave him.

igbo: Ọkịni taka ita, ha atọọ ahịa
english: Trader tells tales, they offer goods.
usage: He says things are cheap, when they are dear.
note: Proverb's exact wording uncertain; 'afià' read as 'ahịa'.
igbo_raw: Qkini tak' ita, watoa afià (Ala).
english_raw: Trader tells tales, they offer goods. He says things are cheap, when they are dear.

igbo: Anya ahụla ya
english: The eyes of people have seen.
usage: When a man denies.
note: OCR 'Ainy' erh' eluo' is badly damaged; the sense points to 'eyes have seen it'.
igbo_raw: Ainy' erh' eluo (0.0.).
english_raw: The eyes of people have seen. When a man denies.

igbo: A mụ na m aka j'akpọ ọjụjụ, ọ jụ ụbọchị atọ
english: If I knew the way to go to pick ojuju, it grows in three days.
usage: To put off a man to whom one is going to do a favour later.
note: 'ototo ato' is probably 'ụbọchị atọ'; the final verb and plant name remain uncertain.
igbo_raw: Amwanam aka j' akp ojuju, ojelu ototo ato (0.0.).
english_raw: If I knew the way to go to pick ojuju, it grows in three days. To put off a man to whom one is going to do a favour later.

igbo: Onye na-enweghị ego si na okwa asọghị ya
english: One who has no money says that okwa does not please him.
usage: Poor man cannot get a wife to cook his yams (sour grapes).
igbo_raw: Onye ne rwen' ego si n'okwa asgroiya (0.0.).
english_raw: One who has no money says that okwa does not please him. Poor man cannot get a wife to cook his yams (sour grapes).

igbo: Otu ọgọ ka ọ na-ama ọnya ilo
english: False accusation pains more than a matchet wound.
note: OCR 'Ofu ogoli k' oinyama elo ilo' is corrupt; the proverb's exact words are uncertain.
igbo_raw: Ofu ogoli k' oinyama elo ilo (0.0.).
english_raw: False accusation pains more than a matchet wound.

igbo: Ebe ọ lụ di ya, ọ na-egbu di ya, were nkpụkpọ tinye n'ọnụ
english: Loved wife kills her husband, takes lamentation and puts it in her mouth.
usage: She pretends.
note: OCR 'Ebq elug diye wel' nkpukpg ti gnp' is badly damaged; 'nkpụkpọ' and 'tinye n'ọnụ' are probable.
igbo_raw: Ebq elug diye wel' nkpukpg ti gnp (0.0.).
english_raw: Loved wife kills her husband, takes lamentation put in mouth. She pretends.

igbo: Azụ nwanyị adịghị akpọ okporo, ọ sịa: ka ya bịakwa
english: Woman's latrine does not call woman, she says: wait a minute.
usage: If a man calls, she makes no excuse.
note: OCR 'Azq grung adakpo okporo, gsja: kaiya biakwa' is uncertain; the final clause is reconstructed from context.
igbo_raw: Azq grung adakpo okporo, gsja: kaiya biakwa (Uk.).
english_raw: Woman's latrine does not call woman, she says: wait a minute. If &i calls, man makes no exeuse.

igbo: Ọ bụ eziokwu na ha gburu enyi, na ha buru isi ya lụọ ụlọ bụ asi
english: (That) they killed the elephant is true, that they carried its head home is a lie.
usage: Of a false accusation.
igbo_raw: Webu envi l' ezie na wa gbu isie lu ung b'asi (Ubul.).
english_raw: (That) they killed the elephant is true, that they carried its head home is a lie. Of a false accusation.

igbo: Anya fụ Oloko ọjọ ihe
english: Oloko met with something.
usage: When a man is tired and wants to go.
note: OCR 'Ainya fy Qlokp oje ife' is unclear; 'ọjọ ihe' is a guess.
igbo_raw: Ainya fy Qlokp oje ife (Ubul.).
english_raw: Oloko met with something: (when a man is tired and wants to go).

igbo: Ọkụkọ abụọ zute udene, ha kpagburu ya.
english: Two fowls meet a vulture, they choke him to death.
usage: When men collect to do something they must do it well.
note: The OCR verb 'watubte' is unrecoverable; the reading follows Thomas's English and the proverb's known shape.
igbo_raw: Qkoko nabi z'udene, watubte (Ubul.).
english_raw: Two fowls meet a vulture, they choke him to death.. When men collect to do something they must do it well.

igbo: Kosi si nne ya n'igbu gbue n'afà; ka ya nye ya nk'onye nwere nwa; ya ga-anwụ, e nye ya ka ọ si adị.
english: Kosi says to mother: you kill him by name; let him bury her as one that has child; when he dies, they bury him as they like.
usage: When a man cannot carry out a plan, he finishes as best he can.
note: 'K'osinadi' and several words are reconstructed from a damaged phonetic transcription.
igbo_raw: Kosi si nneya n'igubugue náfà; kaiya nieye nk'onye nwerwa; ya ganwa wenie K'osinadi (As.).
english_raw: Kosi says to mother: you kill him by name; let him bury her as one that has child; when he dies, they bury him as they like. When a man cannot carry out plan, he finishes as best he

igbo: I banye n'ụlọ onye, a daghị ama àgwà ya.
english: When you reach a man's house, his ways are not known.
usage: When a man has been to a place of bad reputation (really good).
note: The Igbo is reconstructed from damaged OCR; 'El B ónyê' may be a compressed form of 'I banye n'ụlọ onye'.
igbo_raw: El B ónyê, àdämwa àw@ (0.0.).
english_raw: When you reach a man's house, his ways are not known. When a man has been to a place of bad reputation (really good).

igbo: Anaghị m anụ na Ukpebo etuwo tupu akwa m ... m erute.
english: I can't hear that Ukpebo (a stream) rises much and loses cloth till I reach it (while I have not reached it).
usage: Reputation does not frighten one from visiting a man.
note: The proverb is too damaged to recover fully; 'etuke' and 'adeka lue' are especially uncertain.
igbo_raw: Mwano na Ukpebg etuke topu akwa mwa mu adeka lue (Ubul.).
english_raw: I can't hear that Ukpebo (a stream) rises much and loses cloth till I reach it (while I have not reached it). Reputation does not frighten one from visiting a man.

igbo: Omume onye bụ ndụ ya.
english: A man's deeds are his life (good or bad).
note: The Igbo is inferred from the English; the heading 'Ignorance and Knowledge' is omitted as a section title.
igbo_raw: Amal' onye bp mmwa (As.).
english_raw: A man's deeds are his life (good or bad). IgNorance AND KnOWLEDGE.

igbo: Anya adịghị ahụ ntị.
english: The eye cannot see the ear.
note: Restored from OCR 'Áinyd adäff nti'.
igbo_raw: Áinyd adäff nti (As.).
english_raw: The eye cannot see the ear.

igbo: Onye oshi ma onye o zuru; ma onye o zuru amaghị.
english: A thief knows the man from whom he steals; but the loser does not know (the thief).
note: Thomas's 'osi' is read as oshi and 'ozu' as o zuru; the sense is secure.
igbo_raw: Onye osi amwal' onye ozu: mwa onye ozu amwarg (As.).
english_raw: A thief knows the man from whom he steals; but the loser does not know (the thief).

igbo: Ndị nzuzu na-akwa emo ndị amụma.
english: Fools make a mock at prophets (visionaries).
note: The OCR is badly damaged; restored to the standard form of the proverb.
igbo_raw: Ndi nkafia namy ikbomuna amy (As.).
english_raw: Fools make a mock at prophets (visionaries).

igbo: Ọgụmagana sị na ya dị okpoko; okpoko sị na ya dị ọgụmagana; ha abụọ na-ese okwu.
english: Chameleon says he is older than the hornbill; hornbill says he is older than chameleon; both quarrel.
usage: When ọgụmagana was born, earth was muddy, so he goes slowly; hornbill said that there was no earth when he was born, and buried his mother in his head. A book-savvy man is older than an ignoramus.
note: Restored ọgụmagana, okpoko, and ha abụọ na-ese okwu; 'dị' may carry the sense 'older than' in Thomas's dialect.
igbo_raw: Ogumagana si naiya dip okboko; okboko si naiya dig ogumagana; fanebo now'ese (Uk.).
english_raw: Chameleon says he is older than the hornbill; hornbill says he is older than chameleon; both quarrel. When ogumagana was born, earth was muddy, so he goes slowly; hornbill said that there was no earth when he was born, and buried his mother in his head. "Booksavvy" man is older than ignoramus.

igbo: A sị nwata gakpọta nna ya ka o rie ihe; o sị na agụ na-agụ ya, ọ gaghị eje.
english: They say to a child, go and call father to eat; he says he is too hungry to go.
usage: A man who sits at home does not know what they do at the meeting.
note: OCR 'nago ekweroya geje' read as agụ na-agụ ya, ọ gaghị eje.
igbo_raw: Asi rwata gakpota nadiya k'olie ife; osi nago ekweroya geje (Uk.).
english_raw: They say to a child go and call father to eat; he says he is too hungry to go. A man who sits at home does not know what they do at the meeting.

igbo: Nwanna dị onye k'okwe j'ụbe anwa mw'ọda.
english: A kinsman is one who takes a stick to pick an ube (plum) and finds it when it falls.
usage: A witness must be conversant with the case.
note: The Igbo remains uncertain; OCR and Thomas's transcription are too damaged to recover the proverb confidently.
igbo_raw: Nwanna di onye k'okwe j'ube anwa mw'qda (0.0.).
english_raw: Kin (brethren of one) one takes pick ube (plum) and find it when it falls. Witness must be couversant with case.

igbo: Onye dị ụra adịghị eje akaebe.
english: One who sleeps does not go as witness.
usage: Those who have not been to see don't know.
note: Restored ụra for Thomas's 'ola' and akaebe for the missing witness term.
igbo_raw: Onye di ola adesi eli (0.0.).
english_raw: Who sleeps does not go as witness. Those who have not been to see don't know.

igbo: Ihe onye ma ka egwu n'ahịa; ihe onye na-amaghị, ọ na-ajụ ya n'ahịa.
english: Not to know.
note: English is lost beyond 'not know'; the Igbo is a tentative reconstruction from badly damaged OCR.
igbo_raw: Ife ouye mwa ka gégji n'afia; ife onye namwarg odacoïiya n'afia (Uk.).
english_raw: not know.

igbo: Anya onye hụrụ, ọ gaa obi.
english: A man's eyes are witness; he goes to obi.
usage: No one knows without being told.
note: OCR 'luke' read as hụrụ; 'obi' kept as in Thomas.
igbo_raw: Ainya onye luke, og' obi (Uk.).
english_raw: A man's eyes are witness, he goes to obi. No one knows without being told.

igbo: Ụbọchị onye ma ihe niile ka ọ nwụọ.
english: The day one knows all, let him die.
usage: One can always learn.
note: Restored Ụbọchị and niile from OCR.
igbo_raw: Obosi onye mw'as' ife k'onwu (0.0.).
english_raw: The day one knows all let him die. One can always learn.

igbo: Ngwere nwa sị, 'Ọsọ ụtụtụ bụ ọsọ.'
english: The lizard said, running in the morning is running.
usage: It is hard to learn late in life.
note: OCR 'ototo' read as ụtụtụ; 'ngwelanwa' as ngwere nwa.
igbo_raw: Ngwelanwa si n' qsg ototo bu gsg (As.).
english_raw: The lizard said running in morning is running. It is hard to learn late in life.

igbo: Ijiji ji akwa; ngwere bu akwa, ọ gba ọtọ.
english: The fly ties a cloth; the lizard is big enough for a cloth, but goes naked.
usage: When people are tired of a long meeting, carrying out one's plans.
note: Restored ngwere for igwele; abwaloto read as ọ gba ọtọ.
igbo_raw: Ijiji ji akwa; igwele bw' akwa abwaloto (Uk.).
english_raw: The fly ties a cloth; the lizard is big enough for a cloth, but goes naked. When people are tired of long meeting. CArryIng OUt One's PLanS.

igbo: Aka nkpụnkpụ naara mbe ụzọ.
english: A short hand takes away the tortoise's path.
usage: When two people make a plan and one does not carry it out for want of money.
note: nwanega read as mbe; ote as ụzọ.
igbo_raw: Aka nkpunkpu nalo nwanega ote (As.).
english_raw: A short hand takes away tortoise's path. When two people make a plan and one does not carry it out for want of money.

igbo: Ọdịda na-ara ije n'azụ.
english: Falling causes the journey to go back.
note: Ada read as Ọdịda; n'azy as n'azụ.
igbo_raw: Ada nàrá ije n'azy (Ala).
english_raw: Falling causes the journey to go back.

igbo: Mmiri ka eze.
english: Rain is more than the king.
usage: The chief's orders cannot be carried out if natural causes prevent.
note: Mili corrected to Mmiri; O.O. expanded.
igbo_raw: Mili ká éze (0.0.).
english_raw: Rain is more than the king. The chief's orders cannot be carried out if natural causes prevent.

igbo: Aka nkpụnkpụ ekweghị oke kpụọ ụzọ.
english: A short hand does not let a rat cut a path.
usage: When one does not carry out plans owing to illness.
note: ogini read as oke; kw'ote as kpụọ ụzọ.
igbo_raw: Aka nkpunkpu ekwerg ogini kw'ote (Ala).
english_raw: A short hand does not let a rat cut a path. When one does not carry out plans owing to illness.

igbo: Isi eruteghị ebe ọ na-aga, ọ kwụsịghị.
english: If the head does not reach the place it is going to, it does not stop.
usage: Even if a man is hindered by others he fulfils his destiny.
note: OCR badly damaged; reconstructed from English; exact wording uncertain.
igbo_raw: Isi dikelu eB ojeko, gdakwulo (Ala).
english_raw: If the head does not reach place it goes to, it does not stop. Even if a man is hindered by others he fulfils his destiny.

igbo: Onye na-ekwu na ya ga-eri nnukwu taa, na-atụkwasị ezé ya obi.
english: One who says he will eat much more today trusts his teeth.
note: OCR too damaged to recover Thomas's exact transcription; restored known proverb from English.
igbo_raw: Melikçta éekume çzè (0.0.).
english_raw: One who says he will eat much more to-day trusts his teeth.

igbo: Onye nta gburu enwe, bepụ ọdụ ya; ego ya ebelata.
english: If a hunter kills a monkey and cuts off its tail, his money comes short.
usage: When a man dies his plans come to nothing.
note: OCR severely damaged; restored from English and known proverb; Orhle read as Onye nta.
igbo_raw: Orhle Bu grwe obepu qdoa; egoe ebebenoa (Uk.).
english_raw: If a hunter kills monkey and cuts off its tail; his (its ?) money comes short. When a man dies his plans come to nothing.

igbo: Anyị na ị mabe nkakwụ na ijiji; ijiji anwụ akwa, abụba agụ akwụ arụ.
english: We and you will not do as flies and yamstick; the stick holds insects' wings, the wings drop off.
usage: You can't kill a man because he does not know.
note: OCR and Thomas's transcription are too damaged to recover the proverb with certainty.
igbo_raw: Ainyi nai mame nkâkwü na oniji; oniji anw' akwa aboba agu akwu aru (Ubul.).
english_raw: We and you will not do as flies and yamstick; the stick holds insects' wings, the wings drop off. You can't kill a man because he does not know.

igbo: Bịa ka m gwa gị ihe na-akụ nti ọkọ.
english: Come and I'll tell you something that tickles the ear.
usage: One that does not begin cannot finish.
note: The word ihe is not clearly present in the OCR and is restored from sense.
igbo_raw: Bia ka ngwaii nakg nti qko (Uk.).
english_raw: Come and I'll tell you, tickles the ear. One that does not begin cannot finish.

igbo: Ọgụ kwarụ, ọrụ abụrụ.
english: If the hoe handle breaks, the work is spoilt.
usage: When a promise cannot be carried out on account of sickness.
note: Ọgụ is read from Thomas's damaged Agwe; hoe handle is implied by the sense.
igbo_raw: Agwe kwaru, oly aburu (Ubul.).
english_raw: If the hoe handle breaks, the work is spoilt. When a promise cannot be carried out on account of sickness.

igbo: Ụbè ruru enyi ka e ji atọ.
english: It is the spear that suits the elephant that they take to spear it; a gift must be suitable.
note: ruru is restored from the known proverb; Thomas's efulu is unclear.
igbo_raw: Übe' efulu ênyi k'awaji atoa (0.0.).
english_raw: (It is) spear that suits elephant that they take to spear it. Gift must be suitable.

igbo: A dịghị eji okwu abụọ afịa nwaanyị, ekwe na-abụ.
english: People don't flatter a woman twice and have connection.
usage: When a man persuades a boy by promises not carried out.
note: The proverb is only partly recoverable; the OCR and phonetic spelling obscure several words.
igbo_raw: Adewa afia okpôrho ala ekbo nabp (0.0.).
english_raw: People don't flatter a woman twice and have connection. When a man persuades a boy by promises not carried out.

igbo: Okenye takịta, ha tụ afịa.
english: Traders tell many tales, they give them money (wares) to sell or exchange.
usage: If a man gives a trader money in consideration of promises and loses by it.
note: The reading Okenye takịta, ha tụ afịa is tentative.
igbo_raw: Okene takêta, fa tu afia (O.0.).
english_raw: Traders tell many tales, they give them money (wares) (to sell or exchange). If man gives a trader money in consideration of promises and loses by it.

igbo: Okpanam si na ha asụ ebune, na ha eri atụrụ.
english: Okpanam says they forbid ram and eat sheep.
usage: Of a man who takes gifts from an enemy.
igbo_raw: Okbalam si na wa' asp ebunu, na wa eli atuly (Uk.).
english_raw: Okpanam says they forbid ram and eat sheep. Of man who takes gifts from enemy.

igbo: Ije dim unu adịghị eli ọgọ.
english: "I am in a hurry" does not get a present.
usage: Extravagance.
note: adịghị eli ọgọ is restored from adeli ogo; the word for present is uncertain.
igbo_raw: " Ije dim unu " adeli ogo (As.).
english_raw: "I am in a hurry" does not get a present. ExtRAvAGANcE.

igbo: Onye karị onye na-ara ihe o nwere; ọ dị ka onye jide.
english: One who surpasses another takes what he has; it is as if he gives him things to hold.
note: First word and 'na-ara ihe o nwere' restored from damaged OCR.
igbo_raw: Qk' onye nánd if' oiwe; odik' onye jide (Ala).
english_raw: One who surpasses another takes what he has; it is as if he gives him things to hold.

igbo: Onye karị onye emeri ya.
english: One that surpasses another prevails.
note: Cross-reference 'Cf. 387, 439' omitted; 'emeliye' read as emeri ya.
igbo_raw: Onye k'onye emeliye (0.0.).
english_raw: One that surpasses another prevails. Of. 387, 439.

igbo: Otu onye ije, ọ tọọ gọọ.
english: One goes, it bends.
usage: When one is summoned and two come (one as witness).
note: OCR too damaged to recover the proverb with certainty.
igbo_raw: Ofu onye iyele gtogoii (0.0.).
english_raw: One goes, it bends. When one is summoned and two come (one as witness).

igbo: Akpatakpị sị na ya tinye isi n'ite; ma ọ baraghị ọbara, a maghị ewete ya.
english: White-headed lizard says he puts his head in pot; if it is not red, he cannot take it from pot.
usage: A strong man must drive his enemy before he returns.

When people agree to combine and some try to escape subse- quent palaver.

english: They do not carry a house and run if war does not cause it.
usage: When two ebo quarrel and one is much stronger.
note: Restored 'agba ọsọ'; 'ife' in the transcription is read as part of 'ma ọ bụghị'.
igbo_raw: Fadebu ung abwosg ife pgo emero (Ala).
english_raw: They do not carry a house and run if war does not cause it. When two ebo quarrel and one is much stronger.

igbo: Ogo ahụghị ihe ọ ga-eri; ọ na-ewere amara tinye di ya.
english: A woman does not see things to give food; she takes charity and puts it for her husband.
usage: When two towns quarrel and wish to make peace.
note: Ogoli read as Ogo; 'gky grhi' uncertain, perhaps ga-eri or ga-eji nye nri.
igbo_raw: Ogoli afun' ife gky grhi; owglu amelele tingelu dieye
english_raw: (0.0.). A woman does not see things to give food; she takes charity put (explain) for her husband. When two towns quarrel and wish to make peace.

igbo: Agha adịghị mma n'ọkpụ izizi.
english: War is not good at cock crow.
usage: When towns wish to make peace.
note: First word is uncertain; it may be ọgụ rather than agha.
igbo_raw: Kpelegede adenamwa n'okba izizi (Ubul.).
english_raw: War is not good at cock crow. When towns wish to make peace.

igbo: Mmadụ anaghị egbu mmadụ ihe na-emegbughị ya.
english: A man does not kill a man who did not offend him.
usage: If two towns quarrel. The King of Ishan was asked by a man to kill him: he refused as he had no quarrel; the king put corn on his chest: a fowl ate one and was shot with medicine; the king said the fowl had offended him.
note: Kinz read as King; 'emene' and 'pdebte' restored as anaghị egbu and na-emegbughị.
igbo_raw: Mwady emene mwady ife na pdebte (Ubul.).
english_raw: A man does not kill a man who did not offend him. If two towns quarrel. The Kinz of Ishan was asked by a man to kill him: he refused as he had no quarrel; the king put corn on his chest: a fowl ate one and was shot (with medicine); the king said the fowl had offended him.

igbo: Ka anyị ezi, amaghị onye ezi ekwunyere.
english: Let us go to the yard; we do not know for whom the yard speaks.
usage: When a quarreller refuses to go out in reply to a challenge to wrestle.
note: Restored 'amaghị' and 'ekwunyere' from OCR.
igbo_raw: K'apy ezi amwana onye çzi ekwunyelu (0.0.).
english_raw: Let us go to the yard does not know for whom yard speaks. When a quarreller refuses to go out in reply to a challenge to wrestle.

igbo: Ọnwụ adịghị mfe anwụ.
english: Death is not easy to die.
usage: When people separate quarrellers.
note: 'adekwe' read as adịghị mfe.
igbo_raw: Qrwu adekwe anwu (0.0.).
english_raw: Death is not easy to die. When people separate quarrellers. '710. Okwuwa adeje n'ike (0.0.). The word of the world does not go by strength. To oue in fault, when two quarrel and another intervenes.

igbo: Okwu ụwa adịghị eje n'ike.
english: The word of the world does not go by strength.
usage: To one in fault, when two quarrel and another intervenes.
note: 'adeje' read as adịghị eje.
igbo_raw: Adekwusi okwu (0.0.).
english_raw: All is never said. When quarrel goes on in spite of interveners.

igbo: A dịghị akwụsị okwu.
english: All is never said.
usage: When quarrel goes on in spite of interveners.
note: 'Adekwusi' read as A dịghị akwụsị; English may reflect ekwu okwu niile.
igbo_raw: Ngwele si nwenne; kammwa weli odo kwu okwn n'if' onq kwu.ajoka (As.).
english_raw: Lizard tells brother : it is better to take tail to speak, things mouth speaks are bad. If two quarrel.

igbo: Ana m agbala okwu, jiri abalị lie nne; echi efuo, ụtụtụ okwu atọọla.
english: I run from palaver, yet bury my mother at night; at dawn the matter comes up.
usage: When someone is trying to escape palaver and gets it all the same.
note: Restored abalị from OCR uciëi and lie from ni; atọọla from atoloku.
igbo_raw: Anam abwaloku ji uciëi ni nne; ei efuzo ototo okwu atoloku (As.).
english_raw: "I run from palaver " buries his mother at night; at dawn the matter comes up. When someone is trying to escape palaver and gets it all the same.

igbo: Abụzọ sị, ka ya saa ala izu ike; ọ maghị na onye dị n'ala, ọ bụ ọnwụ.
english: The cricket says let him go to the earth to rest; he does not know that whoever goes to earth, it is death.
usage: When someone tries to escape palaver and gets it all the same.
note: saa ala read from si ani; ọnwụ from gnwu.
igbo_raw: Abuzo si keya si ani ezulike; omwarg n'onye di ani, qbul gnwu (As.).
english_raw: Cricket says let him go to the earth to rest ; he does not know that who goes to earth, it is death (i.e., dies). When someone tries to escape palaver and gets it all the same.

igbo: Amara n'amara zụa ahịa, adịghị esu okwu.
english: Acquaintance and acquaintance trade, there is no palaver.
usage: When friends quarrel, outsiders say friends must decide.
note: Thomas's amwale read as amara.
igbo_raw: Amwale n'amwale zua afia adesu okwu (As.).
english_raw: Acquaintance and acquaintance trade, there is no palaver. When friends quarrel, outsiders say friends must decide.

igbo: Egede adịghị ezi ka Ọmadọmwa si kee ya.
english: The drum is not as Ọmadọmwa ties it.
usage: To cowardly soldiers. These proverbs are 'blown' on an ivory horn.
note: Qmadomwa read as Ọmadọmwa; siwekwe as si kee ya.
igbo_raw: Egede adenqzi ka Qmadomwa siwekwe (As.).
english_raw: The drum is not as Qmadomwa ties it. To cowardly soldiers. These proverbs are " blown" on an ivory horn.

igbo: Onịka Ezechi, egwu atụ m.
english: Onịka, son of Ezechi, I fear.
usage: Recalling soldiers after losses.
note: Oniõa read as Onịka; atomam as atụ m.
igbo_raw: Oniõa Ezeci n'egwu atomam (0.0.).
english_raw: Onica (son of) Ezeci I fear. Recalling soldiers after losses.

igbo: Ọzọ maara ọrụ, na-egbu igwe; ọzọ amaghị ọrụ, ọ ma afụ.
english: If a blacksmith understands work, he cuts iron; if he does not, he will gain nothing.
usage: Warning to watch.
note: OCR badly damaged; blacksmith and work words uncertain.
igbo_raw: Ozo mwal okbo obel' igwe; ozo amwan' okóo, omafy,
english_raw: elele nine (0.0.). If a blacksmith understands work, he cuts iron; if he does not, he will gain nothing. Warning to watch,

igbo: Ọdịa oke eme nri.
english: The disgrace of a rat spoils food.
usage: If enemies are prevailing.
note: Oya okg read as Ọdịa oke.
igbo_raw: Oya okg émé nni (0.0.).
english_raw: Disgrace of rat spoils food. If enemies are prevailing.

igbo: Anya gị ene eke, gị ene Ọgụlụgụ.
english: Let eyes see rainbow (see oil palm poles); (Eke Ọgụlụgụ = rainbow) see 176.
usage: When enemy tries to take away body.
note: OCR and transcription uncertain; Ọgụlụgụ restored from Ügulugu.
igbo_raw: Ainya genene eke gene Ügulugu (0.0.).
english_raw: Let eyes see rainbow (see oil palm poles),* (Eke Ögulugu = rainbow) вee 176. When enemy tries to take away body.

igbo: O tọọ bụ ike nwata; chi lọọ jikọ agwa.
english: It tires; telling a quarrelsome man he will be tired before they reply to him.
note: OCR badly damaged; the Igbo reading and English sense are uncertain.
igbo_raw: Otótò bu ike nwata ; ciloa jk' agwa (Ala).
english_raw: tires. Telling quarrelsome man he will be tired before they reply to him.

igbo: Otu onye siri ala, ala gụsịrị; ala siri otu onye, ọ gụsịghị.
english: One cooks for the town, they eat it up; the town cooks for one man, he does not finish it; a man cannot fight the whole town.
note: Restored 'ani' to 'ala' and the OCR fragment 'gdelisi' to 'ọ gụsịghị'.
igbo_raw: Ofu onye sielu ani, ani glisie; n'ami sielu ofu onye
english_raw: gdelisi (0.0.). One cooks for the town, they eat it up; the town cooks for one man, he does not finish it. A man cannot fight the whole town.

igbo: Ọ fọrọ ntịntị ka mkpịsị aka ruo imi.
english: There remains little for the finger to reach the nose.
usage: Of a man who narrowly escapes palaver, or condemnation; it was a narrow shave (of a man escaping ambush).
note: First word OCR 'Okulu' read as 'Ọ fọrọ' from the sense; 'mwa' restored as 'ka'.
igbo_raw: Okulu nwantinti mwa' nkpesi aka abù n'imi (As.).
english_raw: There remains little for the finger to reach the nose. Of a man who narrowly escapes palaver, or condemnation. It was a narrow shave (of man escaping ambush).

igbo: Ọ bụrụ na onye hụrụ onye, ihe ọ na-eme adị mma.
english: If one likes a person, the things he does please one.
usage: Of one who raises objections because he does not like the proposer.
note: OCR 'If' onye s'onye, jf' ome aidimwa' restored from the English.
igbo_raw: If' onye s'onye, jf' ome aidimwa (As.).
english_raw: If one like a person, the things he dues please one. Of one who raises objections because he does not like the proposer.

igbo: Iyi ya kọ bụọ, ọ ga-aka gwoa.
english: His losses surpass his companion's, that is, surpass his company.
usage: If two quarrel, one of whom has lost much, a third may rebuke the other one thus.
note: OCR too damaged; the Igbo reading is a best guess.
igbo_raw: Iyi kobwó, j? àká ghoa (As.).
english_raw: His losses surpass his companion's, (takes to) surpass his company. If two quarrel, one of whom has lost much, a third may rebuke the other one thus.

igbo: Etule kpọọ mgbada, elu Ebudu.
english: To track a duiker reaches Ebudu bush.
usage: To cut palaver short rather than follow it up is to find a worse matter.
note: OCR 'pkwy mbwada' restored as 'kpọọ mgbada'; 'Ebudu' retained as a place name.
igbo_raw: Etul'pkwy mbwada elu ebudu.
english_raw: To track duiker reaches Ebudu bush. To cut palaver short rather than follow it up is to find a worse matter.

igbo: Onye kwara n'oke, ọ dịghị eghe ya rie.
english: One who is free from rat never roasts it and eats; only children eat rats, adults cannot.
usage: When foolish palaver is brought before men.
note: OCR 'qdaro lizie' restored from the English sense; the Igbo is uncertain.
igbo_raw: Onyekwa n'oke qdaro lizie (As.).
english_raw: One who is free from rat never roasts it and eats. Only children eat rats, adults cannot. When foolish palaver is brought before men.

igbo: Anyị amasị ajọ ụzọ banye n'ọhịa.
english: We don't take a bad road to go to the bush.
usage: A man avoids palaver if he can.
note: OCR 'aÿ' read as 'ajọ' and 'oifia' as 'ọhịa'.
igbo_raw: Ainyi amasi aÿ uzo bain' oifia (O.0.).
english_raw: We don't take a bad road to go to the bush. A man avoids palaver if he can.

igbo: Isama, ọ bụ ọgụ, isi ya apịtị.
english: Isama, the fighting place becomes muddy.
usage: When an enemy tries to surround them.
note: OCR 'obwogy isia apiti' likely represents 'ọ bụ ọgụ, isi ya apịtị', but the sense is uncertain.
igbo_raw: Isama, obwogy isia apiti (0.0.).
english_raw: Isama, fighting place becomes muddy. When enemy tries to surround then.

igbo: Akwụ akọ amụlụ amala.
english: Care (kind of food) gently (paddle).
usage: Warning to soldiers.
note: OCR badly damaged; the restoration is tentative and the proverb's sense remains doubtful.
igbo_raw: Akg' akò amûl' amälà (0.0.).
english_raw: Care (kind of food) gently (paddle).* Warning to soldiers.

igbo: Nwata lọọ ọkwa, ya anọ oji.
english: A child picks okwa, let him not pick kola.
usage: When people gather to light and say there is nothing to prevent them.
note: OCR 'lolo okbà, ya on' oji' is uncertain; 'lọọ' and 'anọ' are probable readings.
igbo_raw: Nwata lolo okbà, ya on' oji (0.0.).
english_raw: Child picks okba, let him not pick kola. When people gather to light and say there is nothing to prevent them.

igbo: Oke akwọghị aka, ọ na-eri nri.
english: The rat does not wash its hands when it eats food.
usage: If someone tries to stop men from going to war.
igbo_raw: Oke akwon'aka obelie uni (0.0.).
english_raw: Rat does not wash his hand when he eats food. If someone tries to stop men from going to war.

igbo: A na-egbu ewu maka ọkụkọ?
english: Is a goat killed for a hen?
usage: Rather than fail in war, let a man die.
note: Thomas's 'Etibu' likely represents 'A na-egbu' or 'E gbu'.
igbo_raw: Etibu ewu mwaka pkoko ? (0.0.).
english_raw: Is a goat killed for a hen? Rather than fail in war let a man die.

igbo: Ụkwa daa ọfụma, ọ dịghị ekwe ekwe.
english: The breadfruit falls well, it never shakes.
usage: A good decision settles a case.
note: OCR 'Okwa dà ofuma odefi ekbeleke' restored as 'Ụkwa daa ọfụma, ọ dịghị ekwe ekwe'.
igbo_raw: Okwa dà ofuma odefi ekbeleke (Ubul.).
english_raw: Bread fruit falls well, it never shakes. A good decision settles a case.

igbo: A naghị ebu nwa dị n'afọ nye di.
english: They don't take a child in the womb and give it to a husband.
usage: Don't decide an unheard case.
note: Thomas's 'Wadebue' may reflect 'Ha adịghị ebu' or 'A naghị ebu'.
igbo_raw: Wadebue nwa di afg eke di (Uk.).
english_raw: They don't take child in womb give to husband. Don't decide an unheard case.

igbo: Anụ na-alọghị jiri Oye chọọ akọ.
english: What am I doing? (workless man) takes Oye day to find nuts.
usage: When one wishes to hurry over a case.
note: OCR 'Animaloge ji olie ègg' ako' is very uncertain; the exact wording and meaning remain doubtful.
igbo_raw: Animaloge ji olie ègg' ako (As.).
english_raw: What am I doing ? (workless man) takes Oye day to find nuts. When one wishes to hurry over a case. * Some of these words are used metaphorically; the ordinary meaning is put in brackets.

igbo: Ozi ekwe, ozi ala.
english: Drum judges, drum decides.
usage: When a case is decided in the absence of one party.
note: Restored 'ekwe' and 'ala' from Thomas's 'ekbe' and 'àrhá'; ignored stray 'WRONGDOING' as a section heading.
igbo_raw: Ozi ekbe, ozi àrhá (0.0.).
english_raw: Drum judges, drum decides. When a case is decided in the absence of one party. WROnGDOING.

igbo: Okutulie, ife nụ adị m gị, bialu betolefe n'Obwawo, we ko lu a banye lu Jidaka, ife gkuru ka e jidaka.
english: Okutulie, things of the world are not finished, comes to Tolefe at Obwawo, ready to go calls to Jidaka, things are said that he may hold that.
usage: When a man goes a message, let him take care what he says.
note: OCR and transcription are too damaged to recover a reliable proverb; proper names and verbs remain uncertain.
igbo_raw: Okutulie, ifenu adimgsi, bialu betolefe n'Obwawg, wekoloua bainye lu jidaka, ife gkulu kai ejidaka (As.).
english_raw: Okutulie, things of world are not tinished, comes to Tolefe at Obwawo, ready to go calls to Jidaka, things are said that he may hold that. When a man goes a message, let him take care what he says.

igbo: A na-ebupụ okwu, a dị ebupụ onye ekwu.
english: They carry away the palaver but not the talker.
usage: A man is not punished for threats.
note: Restored final 'onye ekwu' from OCR 'okwu eni'.
igbo_raw: Anebupu okwu adebupu okwu eni (As.).
english_raw: They carry away the palaver but not the talker. A man is not punished for threats.

igbo: Onye fụ ihe a fụ n'anya, o mee ihe a na-emebeghị.
english: When a man sees what he cannot endure, he has done something that they have not seen before, i.e., something wrong.
note: The second clause is uncertain; Thomas's 'emenene' may represent 'a na-emebeghị' or a similar negative form.
igbo_raw: Onye fy afunene ome emenene (As.).
english_raw: When a man sees what he cannot endure, he has done some- thing that they have not seen before, ie., something wrong.

igbo: OkBöko fy eyi gfifie, m'odo; grwe n'ebe qne n'enu z'gdo, ngabu osisi isi adapu, tibue nwa Obu; Obu si na ei amafy.
english: (Bird) sees rat in the day, blows trumpet; monkey where he lives in tree answers trumpet, branch falls, kills child of Obu; Obu says dawn will not come; Obu refuses sympathy; fowl asks why; 'look at her, her children are killed,' Obu accepts her sympathy, etc.
usage: When a man sees what he never saw before (cannot endure), people say it is nothing new; why does he do something wrong?
note: Long tale-proverb is too garbled to restore; Thomas's transcription kept with minor OCR cleanup.
igbo_raw: OkBöko fy eyi gfifie, m'odo; grwe n'ebe qne n'enu z'gdo, ngabu osisi isi adapu, tibue nwa Obu; Obu si na ei amafy (As.).
english_raw: (Bird) sees rat in the day, blows trumpet; monkey where he lives in tree answers trumpet, branch falls, kills child of Obu; Obu says dawn will not come. Obu refuses sympathy ; fowl asks why; "look at her, her children are killed," Obu accepts her sympathy, etc. When a man sees what he never saw before (cannot endure), people say it is nothing new; why does he do something wrong?

igbo: Onye aghụghọ nwụrụ, gwa onye aghụghọ lie ya.
english: A cunning man dies, they take a cunning man to bury him.
usage: A man who does things in secret and is not found out.
note: Restored 'aghụghọ' from OCR 'aiyiyg' and 'lie ya' from 'nie'.
igbo_raw: Ony' aiyiyg nwuru gwelu ony' aiyiyg nie (As.).
english_raw: A cunning man dies, they take a cunning man to bury him. A man who does things in secret and is not found out.

igbo: Ọ dị m iwe na-egbu nwa agụ.
english: "I am troubled" kills the leopard's child.
usage: To a man who breaks law.
note: Restored 'iwe' and 'agụ' from OCR 'iry' and 'nwago'.
igbo_raw: Qdim iry nébu nwago (Ala).
english_raw: " I am troubled " kills the leopard's child. To man who breaks law.

igbo: Ụra gbuo onye; ma uche agbughị ya: uche gbuo onye, ọ na-anwụ.
english: Sleep kills one; thought will not kill him; thought kills him, he dies.
usage: When a man acts against better thoughts.
note: Restored 'Ụra', 'uche', and 'agbughị ya' from Thomas's 'Olu', 'uce', and 'gebune'.
igbo_raw: Olu Bu onye; mw° uce gebune: uce Bu onye, omgrwu (Ala).
english_raw: Sleep kills one; thought will not kill him; thought kills him, he dies. When a man acts against better thoughts.

igbo: Ji ga-amaka mma ruo ọdọ.
english: The yam will be good when you get to the end.
usage: If a friend embezzles.
note: Thomas's 'Abana' is likely the Ika word for yam, restored as 'Ji'; 'gamwakwa mwa' read as 'ga-amaka mma'; 'pdoa' as 'ọdọ'.
igbo_raw: Abana gamwakwa mwa lue pdoa (I.A.).
english_raw: The yam will be good when you get to the end. If a friend embezzles.

igbo: Ngwere abwala ụlọ, ọ jekwaghị akwụkwọ.
english: Lizard breaks his house because he does not go to cut leaf.
usage: Of a guardian who embezzles and neglects.
note: 'Ngwele' normalized to 'ngwere'; 'ung' to 'ụlọ'; 'akukwg' to 'akwụkwọ'.
igbo_raw: Ngwele abwak ung, ojekg akukwg (Ubul.).
english_raw: Lizard breaks his house (because) he does not go (to cut) leaf. Of a guardian who embezzles and neglects.

igbo: Ọsọ gwụ onye ogbu n'ọnụ, mbia okolu ọrịrị.
english: Excuse finishes in the mouth of a murderer; he is ready to hang.
note: Second clause is uncertain; 'qõo' read as 'ọgbu', 'onq' as 'ọnụ', but 'mbia okolu orhirho' is not fully recoverable.
igbo_raw: Osa gwy onye qõo n' onq, mbia okolu orhirho (Ala).
english_raw: Excuse finishes in the mouth of a murderer; he is ready to hang.

igbo: Ọrịa ka dike; ọ karịa onye, emerie ya.
english: Illness is stronger than a strong man; what is stronger than a man conquers him.
usage: If a well man oppresses a sick man of his own accord.
note: 'Qlie' read as 'Ọrịa'; 'emqlie' as 'emerie ya'; 'obwo' likely 'obi' in 'of his own accord'.
igbo_raw: Qlie ka dike; ok' onye emqlie (Ala).
english_raw: Illness is stronger than a strong man; what is stronger than a man conquers him. If a well man oppresses a sick man of his own obwo.

igbo: Afọ na-enweghị otubo, ivilivi k'ọ bụ.
english: Belly that has no navel, is ivilivi.
usage: Of a man that has no conscience.
note: 'Stubo' read as 'otubo'; 'k' qbp' as 'k'ọ bụ'.
igbo_raw: Afg n'enwerg Stubo ivilivi k' qbp (Ubul.).
english_raw: Belly that has no navel, is ivilivi. Of a man that has no conscience.

igbo: K'ede nka n'enwe nzele, fa adịghị akwụ nkite.
english: How about this has time, they don't do it for nothing.
usage: Of injury from unexpected quarter.
note: The second half is uncertain; 'fadekue nkite' may read differently.
igbo_raw: K' ede nka nenwe nzele, fadekue nkite (Ubul.).
english_raw: "How about this" has time, they dow't do it for nothing. Of injury from unexpected quarter.

igbo: Oje na-eje, onye na-ene.
english: A walker walks, a gazer gazes.
usage: If a wrongdoer catches a wrongdoer.
note: 'Ojê mejè one nene' read as 'Oje na-eje, onye na-ene'.
igbo_raw: Ojê mejè one nene (As.).
english_raw: A walker walks, a gazer gazes. If a wrongdoer catches a wrongdoer.

igbo: Njọ dị n'onye mere.
english: Evil is with the evil doer.
note: 'dili' read as 'dị n'...,' 'mele' as 'mere'.
igbo_raw: Njo dili onye mele (As.).
english_raw: Evil is with the evil doer.

igbo: Onye na-akpọbu onye na-enweghị ike na-akpala onye kere ya.
english: He who oppresses the weak is a reproach to his maker.
note: Restored 'na-enweghị ike' and 'na-akpala'; Thomas's 'keli' is read as 'kere ya'.
igbo_raw: Onye nakpwebu onye nerwer' ikg nakpale onye keli (As.).
english_raw: Who oppresses the weak is a reproach to his maker.

igbo: Otu nkpụ lego n'ala eze.
english: One cowry stopped him from being a king.
usage: If a man does a kindness and then harm.
note: 'lego' is uncertain, and the usage phrase is garbled in the OCR.
igbo_raw: Ofu nkpulego nali eze (As.).
english_raw: One cowry stopped him from being a king. If a man does a kindness and then harm.

igbo: Iyi adịghị eli mbụbụ ọdị.
english: The water does not swallow an unbroken calabash.
note: Thomas cross-refers to No. 526; 'eli' is retained for his dialect form of 'swallow'.
igbo_raw: Iyi adieli mbubu odi (As.).
english_raw: The water does not swallow an unbroken calabash. See No. 526.

igbo: Mmadụ bụ ọdị.
english: When a man's labour is vain.
note: The Igbo is only partly recoverable; Thomas's English appears to be a usage note rather than a literal meaning.
igbo_raw: Mwädg by ódI (O.0.).
english_raw: When a man's labour is vain.

igbo: Ife ha bụ nkịtị adịghị mma.
english: What keeps silence is not good.
usage: When a man suffers in silence. Osa sent a hawk to get meat; he caught a young owl, the owl said nothing; he went to get a chicken, the fowl flew crying after the hawk; the owl was carried back to the nest.
note: Read 'fa' as 'ha' and 'bwa' as 'bụ'; the usage note includes Thomas's illustrative story.
igbo_raw: Ife fa bwa nkiti adirg mwa (Ubul.).
english_raw: What keeps silence is not good. When man suffers in silence. Osa sent a hawk to get meat; he caught a young owl, the owl said nothing; he went to get a chicken, the fowl flew crying after the hawk; the owl was carried back to the nest.

igbo: Onye ndidi nwere awẹ.
english: A patient man has luck.
note: Thomas's 'awéle' is read as 'awẹ'; 'nwe' expanded to 'nwere'.
igbo_raw: Onye ndidi nwe awéle (As.).
english_raw: A patient man has luck.

igbo: Ezi azịza nwayọọ na-ewepu iwe.
english: A soft answer turns away wrath.
note: The final word for 'wrath' is restored as 'iwe'; the OCR 'gnuma' is corrupt.
igbo_raw: Eza aziza nwaiyg newepu gnuma (As.).
english_raw: A soft answer turns away wrath.

igbo: O dila arọọ fụ azị ụwa.
english: He who waits patiently sees the back of the world (i.e., lives long).
usage: To a quick-tempered man.
note: Thomas's 'enu' is read as 'ụwa' to match the English; 'Odili' is expanded to 'O dila'.
igbo_raw: Odili arho fu àzi enu (0.0.).
english_raw: He who waits patiently sees the back of the world (i.e., lives long). To quick-tempered man.

igbo: Ọkpọrọ adịghị eri eri di ya akụ
english: A woman does not eat food her husband gives her (she may not eat what she cooks for her husband).
note: The OCR and Thomas's transcription are too damaged to recover this proverb with certainty; the final word may be akwụ or another form.
igbo_raw: Okporo adeli erhi di akua (0.0.).
english_raw: A woman does not eat food her husband gives her (may not eat what she cooks for husband).

igbo: Mụ na gị na-alụ ọbwa na ewi
english: It is tree and rat that I and you marry as spouse.
usage: If a husband spends more on a wife who has not come to him than on the one he has, the marriage is a tree and rat marriage. Obwa seeds scatter far; ewi thinks there will be more near the tree, but is deceived.
note: The second half of Thomas's transcription is unrecoverable; the proverb is restored only in outline from the English and the obwa/ewi image.
igbo_raw: Mwa di pbwa n'ewi ka mu naii etenanoli (0.0.).
english_raw: (It is) tree and rat that I and you marry as spouse. If husband spends more on wife that has not come to hin than on the one he has, the marriage is a tree and rat marriage. Obwa seeds scatter far; ewi thinks there will be more near tree, but is deceived.

igbo: Di ji na-enye ala, ọ na-enye ọnụ ya
english: The farmer gives to the ground, he gives to his mouth.
usage: Of a stingy man who keeps his wives short, when he asks for another wife.
note: Thomas's ani is normalized to standard ala; onua is read as ọnụ ya.
igbo_raw: Di ji enye ani, onye onua (0.0.).
english_raw: The farmer gives to the ground, he gives to his mouth. Of a stingy man who keeps his wives short, when he asks for another wife.

igbo: Afọ na-ebu okwu; ọ dị ka iwe adịghị n'afọ
english: The stomach conceals the word; it is as if anger is not in the stomach.
usage: If a betrothed wife is taken by A from B, and B passes him without assaulting him.
note: dibue is read as na-ebu, and adewe as adịghị.
igbo_raw: Afg dibue okwu; gdika iwe adewe afo (0.0.).
english_raw: The stomach conceals the word; it is as if anger is not in the stomach. If a betrothed wife is taken by A from B, and B passes him without assaulting him.

igbo: Onye na-asụ asụ kwuo okwu; ọ dị ka ọ na-ete ose gafu di ya
english: A useless woman speaks; it is as though she makes pepper soup that will hurt her husband.
usage: If an unloved wife interrupts conversation.
note: gsu is read as asụ; the opening phrase remains slightly uncertain.
igbo_raw: Onye gsu kwu oku; odik' otel' ose gafu diye (0.0.).
english_raw: A useless woman speaks; it is as though she makes pepper soup that will hurt her husband. If unloved wife interrupts conversation.

igbo: Ọsọ ya adịghị aga ogoli
english: One who cannot bear trouble does not go to a woman.
usage: To one who quarrels with wife.
note: The OCR of the first half is obscure; ogoli is the dialect word for woman.
igbo_raw: Qso ye djeb' ögöli (0.0.).
english_raw: One who cannot bear trouble does not go to a woman. To one who quarrels with wife.

igbo: Ha amaghị afọ ogoli
english: They don't know the stomach (ways) of women.
usage: If a wife leaves a man who says he knows her ways.
note: ä d á mw à is read as amaghị and ogoli is retained as the dialect word for woman.
igbo_raw: Wa ädámwà afo ogoli (0.0.).
english_raw: They don't know the stomach (ways) of women. If a wife leaves man who says he knows her ways.

igbo: Ọ siri ike; ọnya atọọ
english: It is hard; sore spreads.
usage: If a man spends all his substance in bidding against another for a wife.
note: úto is read as ọnya; atoi as atọọ.
igbo_raw: Osik' ike; úto atoi (0.0.).
english_raw: It is hard; sore spreads. If man spends all his substance in bidding against another for a wife.

igbo: Odibo eze bụ eze
english: A king's servant is king.
note: Restored 'Odibo' from 'Odiß' and 'bụ' from 'bp'.
igbo_raw: Odiß eze bp eze (As.).
english_raw: A king's servant is king.

igbo: Nwata bakute eze, ọ lisi
english: Child who runs to king has freedom.
note: 'bwakute' read as 'bakute'; 'olisi' uncertain, perhaps 'ọ dị isi'.
igbo_raw: Nwata bwakute eze olisi (Uk.).
english_raw: Child who runs to king has freedom.

igbo: Obu ome adịghị ebu onye a ga-eji ọrụ ni
english: A witch does not kill one whom they take as slave to bury.
usage: Stranger must go to house of obi; obi's child is a big man.
note: OCR badly damaged; the Igbo is a tentative reading and the usage sentence may belong elsewhere.
igbo_raw: Obwome ádebu onye wa geji oru ni (Uk.).
english_raw: A witch does not kill one whom they take slave to bury. Stranger must go to house of obi; obi's child is a big man.

igbo: Ajali sị: na ya ga-eje gafee Oba nwanne ya; n'ọ bụọ ya, ọ dị mma; n'ọ hapụ ya, ọ dị mma
english: Axe says: he will go to see Oba his brother; if he kills him it is good; if he keeps him it is good.
usage: When a chief calls a young man.
note: OCR merges Igbo and English; 'odomerhie gmwaka' is unrecovered and the proverb is reconstructed from the English.
igbo_raw: Ajali si: naiya geje gafy Oba rwanng; n'obue gmwaka
english_raw: odomerhie gmwaka (I.A.). Axe says: he will go to see Oba his brother; if he kills him it is good; if he keeps him it is good. When a chief calls a young man.

igbo: Aji mụrụ ụmụ, sị: nke bụ ụmụ ya soro ya si mmiri; nke na-abụghị ụmụ ya si elu
english: A crocodile bears children, says her own follow her to the water; those that are not hers go up. (Ngwelanwu (lizard) is said to be child of aji.)
note: Restored from phonetic transcription; 'Ngwelanwu' parenthetical kept as Thomas's note.
igbo_raw: Ajii mul' umy si nke bu umwa sole si mili; nke nebuly umwa si enu (As.).
english_raw: A crocodile bears children, says her own follow her to the water; those that are not hers go up. (Ngwelanwu (lizard) is said to be child of aji.) etc.).

igbo: Okwu eze kwudị onye, ọ nụọ nkpụli iyi
english: The word of the king meets one, he swallows iyi ball (stone).
usage: If the head chief accused a man, the accused admitted his guilt, whether innocent or guilty.
note: 'kwudi' read as 'kwudị'; 'nkpuly' as 'nkpụli'.
igbo_raw: Okwezé kwudi onye, onüe nkpuly iyi (0.0.).
english_raw: The word of the king meets one, he swallows iyi ball (stone). If the head chief accused a man, the accused admitted his guilt, whether innocent or guilty.

igbo: Eze nwe ala
english: The head chief has the land.
usage: When people excuse themselves from coming to the head chief.
note: Restored 'ala' from OCR 'anjnéa'; 'Wheu' repaired to 'When'.
igbo_raw: Eze nwe anjnéa (0.0.).
english_raw: The head chief has the land. Wheu people excuse themselves from coming to head chief.

igbo: Orimili lị onye, ọ lịe ọgụ aya
english: A river drowns one, it drowns his war medicine.
usage: To a reckless man who does not care for his chief.
note: 'Orhimili' read as 'Orimili'; 'olie' as 'ọ lịe'.
igbo_raw: Orhimili 1 li onye, olie ogu aya (0.0.)
english_raw: A river drowns one, it drowns his war medicine. To a reckless man who does not care for his chief.

igbo: Ọsụ ọfịa agwa di ji na afọ na-abịa
english: Osu ofia says to the farmer that the year comes round.
usage: Of people impatient to make new yams (time is fixed by the head chief).
note: The Igbo is damaged; 'na afọ na-abịa' is a guess from the English sense and the OCR 'n'arho aboa'.
igbo_raw: Qsu pifia agwa di ji n'arho aboa (I.A.).
english_raw: Osu oifia says to farmer that the year comes round. Osu oifia is a plant. Of people impatient to make new yams (time is fixed by head chief).

igbo: Aka onye na-ata nkwu na-achụ onye n'ubi
english: The hand of the palm-wine maker drives the maker from the plantation.
usage: When a suitor cohabits with a girl too soon.
note: The OCR leaves the tapper phrase ambiguous; 'n'abo' may stand for n'ubi or another place word.
igbo_raw: Ak' oei naèy oei n'abo (Ubul.).
english_raw: The hand of the palm wine maker drives the maker fron the plantation. When a suitor cohabits with a girl too soon.

igbo: Onye nọrọ n'ọzọ, ọ hụ ọyịa
english: One who sits long with the blacksmith sees his friend.
usage: If an adulterer sits with friends, eats and drinks, the husband may come and catch him.
note: The parenthetical '(A man only buys as much as he wants.)' is omitted as garbled; 'nọrọ' restores Thomas's 'noka'.
igbo_raw: Onye noka n'ozo, ofu oiyia (0.0.).
english_raw: One who sits long with the blacksmith, he sees his friend. (A man only buys as much as he wants.) If an adulterer sits with friends, eats and drinks, the husband may come and catch him.

igbo: Onye gbụ ogene adịghị edo ikè n'otu ebe
english: Who beats the ogene never stands in one place.
usage: If a woman can't stay in one man's house.
note: 'hoes a row' is read as 'beats the ogene'; 'gtili' is restored as 'ebe'.
igbo_raw: Onye gbu ogene adedo ikè n'ofu gtili (I.A.).
english_raw: Who hoes a row never stands in one place. If a woman can't stay in one man's house.

igbo: Ọgọli je n'ụlọ abụọ, ọ ma nke kama ya
english: A woman goes to two houses (e.g. gets two husbands); she knows which is better.
usage: Of a woman that wants to leave her husband.
note: 'Ọgọli' is kept as Thomas's dialect word for woman.
igbo_raw: Ogoli je ung nabg omwale nke kamwa (As.).
english_raw: A woman goes to two houses, (e.g. gets two husbands) she knows which is better. Of a woman that wants to leave her husband.

igbo: Nwunye di na-achọ ihe, nwunye di ya sị akpala ya rie, ka ya akpala rie
english: Find and eat; let her find and eat.
usage: When wife and husband quarrel; 'don't provide for me,' i.e. she finds husband has nothing.
note: The OCR is too damaged to recover the proverb confidently; the reading follows the English and the repeated 'rie'.
igbo_raw: Nwunyedi nefkliye nwunyediye osi akpalilie, kaiya akpalilie (As.).
english_raw: find and eat, let her find and eat. When wife and husband quarrel; "don't provide for me," ¿.e. she finds husband has nothing.

igbo: Mụwa dị ndụ, ọkụkọ nwanyị atụpụ nkem
english: While I live, a fowl of a woman does not bite mine to death.
usage: Of a father who treats the mother badly (e.g. taking away her things to give to another wife).
note: 'mwady' is read as nwanyị, hence 'woman' rather than Thomas's printed 'man'; the verb is uncertain.
igbo_raw: Mmwa dindo pkoko mwady atußue nkem (As.).
english_raw: While I live, a fowl of a man does not bite mine to death. Of afigher giho treans ther inefhe bead kil w tabing. her

igbo: Mụwa dị ndụ, ọkpa nne m anaghị afụ
english: While I live, corn-ball of my mother is not unsold.
usage: Of a father who treats boy's mother badly (e.g. taking away her things to give to other wife).
note: 'okbo' is read as ọkpa and 'anafia' as anaghị afụ.
igbo_raw: Mwa dindo okbo nnem anafia (As.).
english_raw: While I live, corn-ball of my mother is not unsold. Of a father who treats boy's mother badly (e.g. taking away her things to give to other wife).

igbo: Achọ di na achọ nwunye adịghị ezute n'ụzọ.
english: One seeking a husband and one seeking a wife never meet on the road.
usage: When a man has money and cannot find a wife; after spending his money he finds a suitable wife.
note: OCR '0.0.' expanded as O.O.; restored 'adịghị ezute' from 'ádezu'.
igbo_raw: Aëgko di na aèqko nwunye ádezu n'uzg (0.0.).
english_raw: One seeking husband and one seeking wife never met on the road. When a man has money and can't find a wife; after spend- ing his money he finds a suitable wife.

igbo: Bụta bụta eyim okwu, ma ọ bụghị akwa.
english: A running man is like a call, not a cry.
usage: When a woman mourns her husband.
note: Obscure Asaba wording; 'eyim' and 'bụta bụta' uncertain.
igbo_raw: Bwata bwata eyiem okwu m'oburg ákwá (As.).
english_raw: A running man is like a call, not a cry. When a woman mourns her husband.

igbo: Akwụkwọ ogede na-eme lama lama; dịka onweghị ndọka.
english: Plantain leaf is shining as though it does not tear.
usage: To a virgin who refuses a husband and cares for no man.
note: Restored 'akwụkwọ' and 'na-eme'; 'ndọka' remains uncertain.
igbo_raw: Akukwg ogede neme lama lama; gdika onwerg ndoka (As.).
english_raw: Plantain leaf is shining as though it does not tear. To a virgin who refuses husband and cares for no man.

igbo: Anya akpọ nni na-eri nwe ya, n'isi onye nwe ya ka ọ na-aga, ọ dịghị efu.
english: Eyes that spoil go to the head of the owner and are not lost.
usage: When a wife bears no children; she has other work.
note: Final clause inferred from English; 'akpọ nni' uncertain.
igbo_raw: Ainyakbo nni na dinweniye n'isi n' oyir(g) eyi (As.).
english_raw: Eyes that spoil go to head of owner and are not lost. When wife bears no children; she has other work.

igbo: Omi dịghị ebu mmiri, ọ ga-ebu ntọ.
english: A well that does not hold water will hold ashes.
usage: When a man's wife bears no children, he does not repudiate her.
note: Thomas's 'ana' rendered as standard 'ebu'.
igbo_raw: Omi dikana mili ogana nto (Uk.).
english_raw: A well that does not hold water, will hold ashes. When a man's wife bears no children, he does not repudiate her.

igbo: Azụ nwere mmiri, ma ọ hụghị ncha ọ ga-eji asa ahụ.
english: A fish has water but sees no soap to wash with.
usage: A farmer may have many yams but no wife.
note: Restored 'nwere', 'hụghị', 'ncha', 'asa ahụ' from OCR.
igbo_raw: Azq-nwe mili, mw' pdafy néa oji awp ary (Ala).
english_raw: A fish has water but sees no soap to wash with. A farmer may have many yams but no wife.

igbo: Akwụ leni buru ọka okwu.
english: Rotten nut brings palaver for the corn.
usage: A woman brings trouble to a man.
note: 'leni' uncertain; likely a dialect word for rotten.
igbo_raw: Akwy leni bur' oka okwu (Uk.).
english_raw: Rotten nut brings palaver for the corn. Woman brings trouble to'man.

igbo: Anyị amaghị ịkpa agụ na ewu; gị bụ onye ọcha, i nwere ike ịkpa agụ na ewu.
english: We cannot tie leopard nor goat; you are a white man, you can tie leopard and goat.
usage: (a) Only a white man can order obi. (b) Leopard and goat (husband and co-respondent) come to court together, eat together.
note: Thomas's 'inibe' taken as ịkpa; 'order obi' left as in Thomas.
igbo_raw: Ainyi amwanwe ikg inibe Awolg nibe ewu; ngi by onye oica rwe ike inibe awolg nib' ewu (Uk.).
english_raw: We cannot tie leopard nor goat; you are a white man, you can tie leopard and goat. (a) Only white man can order obi. b) Leopard and goat (husband and co-respondent) come to court together, eat together.

igbo: Ekwu kwemefu maka ọkwụ m ọkwụ; idụm, amaghị m ebe di m nọ zi.
english: I speak it as a word that is said; idumu, I do not know where my husband is.
usage: Husband has never cohabited with wife, though he does with others.
note: ọkwụ m ọkwụ and idụm are uncertain; OCR damaged the proverb heavily.
igbo_raw: Ekwu kwemefu mak' ökwdmökwú; idumu, amwargn ebe dim nozi (Ubul.).
english_raw: I speak it as a word that is said ; idumu, I do not know where my husband is. Husband has never cohabited with wife, though he does with others.

igbo: Ọkụkọ mma ọma etiwa ite, etiwa obobwa, n'ọ maara ebe ọ na-aga ụra.
english: Fowl wilfully breaks pot, and open pot knows where it goes to sleep.
usage: When a woman runs from her husband, they will return her.
note: Several words in the Igbo are reconstructed from a damaged OCR reading; 'mma ọma' and 'obobwa' remain uncertain.
igbo_raw: Qkoko mwa omwa etiwe ite, etiwe obobwa, n' omwago ebe ojekp alaru (Ubul.).
english_raw: Fowl wilfully breaks pot and open pot knows where it goes to sleep. When woman runs from husband; " they will return her."

igbo: Di adịghị mma, nwunye adịghị mma.
english: A husband is not good, a wife is not good; it is six of one to half a dozen of the other.
note: Thomas's 'adina/adjna' normalized to standard adịghị.
igbo_raw: Di adina mwa nwunye adjna mwa (Ubul.).
english_raw: A husband is not good, a wife is not good. Six of one to half a dozen of the other.

igbo: Ọ dịghị n'ọnụnụ di ya.
english: It is not the same thing to be a lover and to be a husband (perhaps waiting and marrying).
note: The second half of the Igbo is badly damaged; 'ọnụnụ di ya' is a guess at the sense of lover/husband.
igbo_raw: Qdidi n' onyny dièe (As.).
english_raw: It is not the same thing to be a lover and to be a husband. (? Waiting and marrying.)

igbo: Di na nwunye rụrụ ụlọ debe okwu.
english: A husband and wife build a house for palaver.
note: Thomas's 'l' ung' likely represents rụrụ ụlọ or lụrụ ụlọ.
igbo_raw: Di na nwunye l' ung debel' okwu (As.).
english_raw: Husband and wife build house for palaver.

igbo: Nkwụ adịghị aka, pụkwe ike amaghị.
english: Palm tree is not ripe, foot (buttocks) does not know.
usage: The people of an ebo know when a man comes to marry a girl. Secrets.
note: The Igbo is only partly recoverable; 'pụkwe' and the sense of 'aka' are uncertain.
igbo_raw: Nkwi ádäc' akd pkwye (ike) amwarg (As.).
english_raw: Palm tree is not ripe, foot (buttocks) does not know. The people of an ebo know when a man comes to marry a girl. SecRETS.

igbo: Ụmụ welu nye okporo adịghị enwe isi.
english: Counsel they take with a woman has no head.
usage: When a man betrays a secret.
note: The first words are damaged; 'okporo' is taken as woman and the proverb's exact shape is uncertain.
igbo_raw: Ume welunye okporo adenwe ísi (0.0.).
english_raw: Counsel they take with a woman has no head. When a man betrays a secret.

igbo: Oke ọhịa gwa oke ụnụ si na nkpọdo dị n'ọkụ.
english: The bush rat tells the house rat that the (fish) basket is over the fire.
usage: If a man reveals secrets.
note: Restored 'pfia' as ọhịa and 'rgiga' as n'ọkụ; the latter is uncertain.
igbo_raw: Oke pfia gwa oke unq si na nkpodo di na rgiga (As.).
english_raw: The bush rat tells the house rat that (fish) basket is over the fire. If a man reveals secrets.

igbo: Ewu chọrọ itinye ọnu n'olu, ọ hụghị onye ga-ekee ya.
english: A goat wants to put a small calabash on his neck but does not see one to tie it on.
usage: No one can refuse to be made obi at no cost to himself.
note: Restored ewu, chọrọ, itinye, ọnu, n'olu, hụghị, ga-ekee ya from the OCR; the moral was separated as usage.
igbo_raw: Qta dig' çwu k'ozi Qn'onu mw' pfurg onye iyibeni (Ala).
english_raw: A goat wants to put small calabash on his neck but does not see one to tie it on. No one can refuse to be made obi at no cost to himself.

igbo: A dịghị eji ọlọpọ egbochi ụzọ.
english: They don't take olopo tree to shut the road.
usage: If two men are good friends, and a son commits adultery with the wife of one, it does not cause a quarrel.
note: Restored the negative and the verb egbochi from Thomas's Wadeji qlopo nebuci фxQ.
igbo_raw: Wadeji qlopo nebuci фxQ (I.A.).
english_raw: They don't take olopo tree to shut the road. If two men are good friends, and a son commits adultery with the wife of one, it does not cause a quarrel. E

igbo: Ọ bụ ọkẹ taa na-abụ ọrịa; ngwere asị: wazinye ego gọọ ezé.
english: The bite that a rat bites turns to disease; the lizard says: lend him money to file his teeth.
usage: Friends meet at night to talk; then tell a tale that causes laugh.
note: Uncertain readings: Alo taken as Ọ bụ, plie as ọrịa, and wazinye/gọọ ezé as Thomas's dialect forms.
igbo_raw: Alo oke ta nab' plie; ngwel' asj: wazinye ego gow°
english_raw: çze (I.A.). Bite that rat bites turns to disease; lizard says: lend him money to file his teeth. Friends meet at night to talk; then tell a tale that causes laugh.

igbo: Onye na-egbu mbada otu a n'afọ ọzọ.
english: When a hunter kills a duiker, he says "another year" (he will kill).
usage: A friend takes a friend's things and tells him.
note: Restored Orhene Bu mbwada otã n'arh qzg as Onye na-egbu mbada otu a n'afọ ọzọ.
igbo_raw: Orhene Bu mbwada otã n'arh qzg (O.0.).
english_raw: When hunter kills duiker, he says "another year" (he will kill). A friend takes a friend's things and tells him.

igbo: Ewu nọdibe ji, ọ bụrụ rie.
english: If a goat sits near yams it takes and eats.
usage: Cultivate a friend if you want benefactions.
note: Restored obug lie as ọ bụrụ rie; the exact verb form remains slightly uncertain.
igbo_raw: Ewu, nodibe ji, obug lie (0.0.).
english_raw: If a goat sits near yams it takes and eats. Cultivate a friend if you want benefactions.

igbo: Onye na-aga egbụ si udene, akala gịnị i ji efe efe? Ọ bụghị gbụ m, ị gaghị eri m.
english: One who goes to be killed says to the vulture: why do you fly over me? If qba does not kill me, you can't eat me.
usage: If a friend calumniates a son-in-law, a man cannot take away his daughter.
note: The final OCR geli anoa is uncertain; qba is left as Thomas's reading.
igbo_raw: Onye jegebu si udene akala gini ijel ufe, mw'gb ebune
english_raw: geli anoa (0.0.). One who goes to be killed says to vulture: why do you fly over me, if qba does not kill me, you can't eat me. If friend calumniates son-in-law, man cannot take away daughter.

igbo: Akpọ m idide, ọlu ịsụsị ga-eri ya.
english: If they gather worms, the work of cutting bush will eat them.
usage: If friends stay long to talk, the visitor can say this.
note: Restoration of asụsụ/ịsụsị and the verb ending in gelieye is uncertain.
igbo_raw: AkBom' idide, olu asusy gelieye (I.A.).
english_raw: If they gather worms, work of eutting bush will eat them. If friends stay long to talk, the visitor can say this.

igbo: Ha hụ ọkụ ọkọchị, ha wawa ubi.
english: They see the light of a dry season, they cut the farm.
usage: A reply to 807. We will talk again on occasion.
note: Restored Afy ifolo okqëi wawal' ubwo as Ha hụ ọkụ ọkọchị, ha wawa ubi.
igbo_raw: Afy ifolo okqëi wawal' ubwo (I.A.).
english_raw: They see the light of a dry season, they cut the farn. A reply to 807. We will talk again on occasion.

igbo: A na-eche ka ngwere nwee ntutu, anaghị ebe di.
english: They wait for the lizard to get hair, and do not go to a husband.
usage: To get rid of importunate beggar.
note: Restored ngwere and rendered Thomas's 'aku' as ntutu from the English sense; the husband clause remains slightly awkward.
igbo_raw: Aceme ka ngwele bw'aku, anqrho bedi (0.0.).
english_raw: They wait for lizard to get hair, and don't go to a husband. To get rid of importunate beggar.

igbo: A naghị afịa onye kụrụ ntutu.
english: They never flatter one who plants hair.
usage: To importunate borrower.
note: OCR 'Wadafia okba' restored as A naghị afịa onye; 'kụrụ' could also be read kpara in the dialect.
igbo_raw: Wadafia okba ntutu (Ubul.).
english_raw: They never flatter one who plants hair. To importunate borrower.

igbo: A sị onye nzuzu na chi agwụla, ọ na-achọ anyanwụ.
english: They say to the fool that the day is done; he looks for the sun.
usage: When a man is twice refused and persists.
note: OCR 'obwodi' and 'di and' are damaged; the reading follows the known proverb.
igbo_raw: Wasí obwodi na di and; onényo ainyanwu (Ala).
english_raw: They say to the fool that the day is done; he looks for the SUN. • When a man is twice refused and persists.

igbo: A naghị asị Obolo, ọ dịghị ka bụ ebo onye.
english: They do not say Obolo (town) while it is not one's ebo.
usage: To one who interferes with domestic affairs of another.
note: The OCR leaves the negative and the clause structure uncertain.
igbo_raw: Adas' Obolo pdikaby ebo onyefy (Uk.).
english_raw: They don't say Obolo (town), while it is not one's ebo. To one who interferes with domestic affairs of another.

igbo: Ozu ọhụrụ adịghị eme ihe iyi.
english: A fresh corpse is not an ugly sight.
usage: When corpse's relatives do not attend funeral.
note: OCR 'oyiyi' and 'izizi' are uncertain; restored from the English sense.
igbo_raw: Ozq oyiyi ademe izizi (0.0.).
english_raw: A fresh corpse is not an ugly sight. When corpse's relatives do not attend funeral.

igbo: Ozu anaghị anụ isi onwe ya.
english: A dead body cannot smell itself.
note: OCR 'ámy' expanded as anaghị anụ; the exact dialect negative remains uncertain.
igbo_raw: Ozq ámy isi onwe (As.).
english_raw: A dead body cannot smell itself.

igbo: Ihere adịghị eme ozu.
english: A corpse feels no shame.
igbo_raw: Ifele ademe ozu (As.).
english_raw: A corpse feels no shame.

igbo: Agu buru onye, ọ buru onyinyo ya.
english: Leopard carries off someone, it carries his shadow; the shadow dies with the man.
note: Restored 'onyinyo ya' from the OCR 'onyinyue'.
igbo_raw: Agu bul' onye abul' onyinyue (As.).
english_raw: Leopard carries off' someone, it carries his shadow. Shadow dies with man.

igbo: Elibe adakwọ ọnụma.
english: When you eat, you are not vexed.
usage: When a man refuses help but makes use of a friend.
note: qnuma read as ọnụma; Elibe left as Thomas's form.
igbo_raw: Elibe adakw' qnuma (As.).
english_raw: When you eat, you are not vexed. When a man refuses help but makes use of friend. HOME.

igbo: Onye na-enweghị nwunye ya bụ ogbenye nke ebo ya.
english: He who has no wife is the poor man of his ebo.
usage: When a man returns home after work.
note: ikßd di ebo read as ogbenye nke ebo ya; uncertain.
igbo_raw: Onye ninwerg nwunye ya by ikßd di ebo (Ala).
english_raw: Who has no wife is the poor man of his ebo. When a man returns home after work. E 2

igbo: Nti pụa obodo, ọ nụ okwu.
english: Ears go to town and hear a word.
usage: The stay-at-home does not know what happens.
note: gmp oku read as ọ nụ okwu.
igbo_raw: Nti pua obôdo; gmp oku (0.0.).
english_raw: Ears go to town hear a word. The stay at home does not know what happens.

igbo: Ọ dị iche n'ọnọdụ na ibi.
english: Staying in a place and living there are different.
note: Qdidi n' oning diùe read as Ọ dị iche n'ọnọdụ na ibi; uncertain.
igbo_raw: Qdidi n' oning diùe (As.).
english_raw: Staying in a place and living there are different.

igbo: Ọ bụ n'ụtụtụ; ọ gaghị adị mma; ọ bụ ugboro abụọ echi.
english: Let it be in the morning; it will not be good; twice tomorrow.
usage: A man changes his mind after asking a friend to come and finish the matter.
note: Several words are unrecoverable; the reading follows the known proverb shape.
igbo_raw: Onçh' ototo; adadimwa ikpenabg (0.0.).
english_raw: Let it be in the morning; it will not be good; twice (to-morrow). A man changes his mind after asking a friend to come and finish matter.

igbo: Onye nọ n'okwu pụtara ọnụ.
english: He who stays long on a message utters a word.
usage: To those who come to listen unasked.
note: okg read as n'okwu; onp as ọnụ.
igbo_raw: Onye noka okg ptonye onp (Ubul.).
english_raw: Who stays long on message, he utters a word. To those who come to listen unasked.

igbo: Gbadi egwu n'ụlọ, anyị eti ọnụ.
english: The drum is in the house; we beat the mouth.
usage: If one man speaks when another should speak.
note: Gadi egede read as Gbadi egwu.
igbo_raw: Gadi egede uno, ainyi eti ony (I.A.).
english_raw: Drum will be house, we beat mouth. If one man speaks when another should speak.

igbo: Mbe nwere otu akwa, ọ naghị ewe ya akwa.
english: If a tortoise has only one cloth, he does not take it to sew a dress.
usage: To a man who begs for a unique thing.
note: Mbeku read as Mbe; amanwe as nwere; owelekw' awe as ọ naghị ewe ya akwa.
igbo_raw: Mbeku amanwe ofu akwa owelekw' awe (Ubul.).
english_raw: If a tortoise has only one cloth he does not take it to sew" dress. To man who begs for unique thing.

igbo: Aka nkpọnkpọ ekweghị nwa ega kpọọ ụzọ
english: A short hand does not allow a tortoise to make a path.
usage: When a man cannot return a friend's kindness, he is ashamed and loses his friend.
note: Thomas's 'nwanega' (tortoise) and closing verb 'kw'ote' are uncertain, so this clause is restored only tentatively.
igbo_raw: Aka nkponkpo ekwene nwanega kw'ote (0.0.).
english_raw: A short hand does not allow a tortoise to make a path. When a man cannot return a friend's kindness, he is ashamed and loses his friend.

igbo: Okwu dị n'ọnụ ka m ji amara ọyị
english: A word in the mouth is what I take to know a friend.
usage: Said when a friend deceives.
note: Thomas's 'amwa' may represent 'amara' (to know, matching his English) or 'amwa' (to test); 'ọyị' (written 'os)') is his Asaba word for friend.
igbo_raw: Okwu di n' ony ka mji amwa os) (As.).
english_raw: Word in mouth, that I take to know a friend. If friend deceives.

igbo: Ngwele sịrị: ka o weli ọdụ n'ọgụ; onye na-abụ ewere ọnụ kwuo
english: One lizard says to another: let us fight with tails; let neither take his mouth to speak.
usage: When a friend injures a friend, the latter says this.
note: The middle of the proverb (Thomas's 'k'oweli qdo nu ggo; onye nabg ewe n' onu kwu') is badly damaged and the tail-fight and 'mouth to speak' clauses cannot be settled with certainty.
igbo_raw: Ngwele sibè k'oweli qdo nu ggo ; onye nabg ewe n' onu kwu (Uk.).
english_raw: One lizard says to another: let's fight with tails ; let neither take his mouth to speak. When friend injures friend, latter says this.

igbo: Onye were madụ tinye n'iwe abụghị ọyị ya
english: Whoever takes a man and puts him in trouble is not his friend.
note: Thomas's 'mwady' is restored as 'madụ' (person) on the strength of his English 'a man'; 'abprg qsia' is read as 'abụghị ọyị ya' on the pattern of his Asaba friend-word.
igbo_raw: Onye we mwady tinye n'iwele abprg qsia (Uk.)
english_raw: Who takes a man and puts him in trouble is not his friend.

igbo: Mbada sị ibe ya: onye nụ muke muke, ya mụkenye ibe ya, na akpụkpọ ibe ya ka e ji akwụ egwu
english: Duiker says to his kin: whoever hears "hunter" should tell his fellows, because it is his kin's skin they take to make a drum.
usage: Said to a friend who omits to warn [another].
note: The word Thomas glosses 'hunter' ('muke muke') is unrecoverable, and the drum-making clause ('akbukbg ibewe ka waji kwegwu') is doubtful.
igbo_raw: Mbwada si ibewa : onye ny muke muke, ya mukenye ibewe na akbukbg ibewe ka waji kwegwu (Uk.).
english_raw: Duiker says to his kin: who hears "hunter" let him tell his fellows, because skin of his kin they take to make drum. To friend who omits to warn.

igbo: Nwanne ahụgo ụmụ nwanne, ọ ga-edede ụmụ di ya
english: When a sister has seen the children of her sister, she embraces her husband's children.
usage: A man tells his friend, not his brother, and is killed.
note: Thomas's 'Koji gedede' is obscure; it is restored as 'ọ ga-edede' on the strength of his English 'she embraces', but the verb remains uncertain.
igbo_raw: Nwene afugo ump nwene, Koji gedede umudte (Ubul.).
english_raw: When sister has seen the children of her sister, she embraces her husband's children. A man tells his friend, not his brother, and is killed.

igbo: Onye ọrịa enweghị ọyị
english: A sick man has no friend.
note: Thomas's 'os'' is taken as his Asaba spelling of 'ọyị' (friend); the negative 'énw' is read as 'enweghị'.
igbo_raw: Onye olia énw os' (As.).
english_raw: A sick man has no friend.

igbo: Ha na-abụ ọyị dị ka isi na anya
english: They are friends like head and eyes.
usage: The eyes do not see the head; one does not know a friend's secret.
note: The word between 'ọyị' and 'isi' (Thomas's 'neso') is doubtful and is read as 'dị ka'; 'oiyi' is standardised to 'ọyị'.
igbo_raw: Wa nabo neso oiyi isi n' ainya (As.).
english_raw: They are friends like head and eyes. (Eyes don't see head) one doesn't know one's friend's secret.

igbo: Ọnwụ enweghị ebere.
english: Death has no pity.
note: Restored Qrwu/eb¢le as Ọnwụ/ebere and supplied the negative enweghị.
igbo_raw: Qrwu énwe eb¢le (As.).
english_raw: Death has no pity.
